THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | QA Verification Standard — Mesh & Resolution | rev 3 | Effective 07/01/2025
Document ID: CFDME-QA-VS-MR Revision: rev 3 Effective Date: 07/01/2025 Supersedes: rev 2 (Effective
03/15/2023) Author of Record: Marguerite Falk, PE — Technical Director & Reviewing Engineer, AZ PE #42798
Applies To: All CFD deliverables issued from The CFD Mechanical Engineer, LLC (The CFD ME), 4820 E River Rd,
Suite 220, Tucson, AZ 85718
1. Purpose & Scope
This standard establishes the firm's minimum requirements for demonstrating that a CFD result is grid-independent
(for steady Reynolds-averaged work) or adequately resolved (for large-eddy simulation), and specifies how the
underlying evidence must be presented in the Verification section of every deliverable that leaves the firm.
The standard applies to every project executed by The CFD ME staff and to every subcontracted deliverable
prepared on the firm's behalf, including work performed by Mulshi Simulation Labs and any other external contractor
operating under a CFD ME work order. Reviewing Engineer sign-off on the peer-review checklist requires explicit
confirmation that the requirements of this document have been met.
Revision 3 rewrites the LES portion of the standard. The rev 2 language treated the Roache/Richardson grid
convergence index (GCI) as the default verification instrument for every solve regardless of turbulence treatment.
Two internal audits and a client peer review in Q1 2025 established that the treatment is technically incorrect for
large-eddy simulation and produces verification evidence that will not survive third-party scrutiny. The corrected
treatment is set out in Sections 4 and 5.
Nothing in this standard modifies the firm's Validation QA Procedure & Acceptance Criterion
(Firm/QA/CFDME_Validation_Procedure_rev2), the firm's Modeling Standards for Fire & Buoyant Flows
apply concurrently.
2. Definitions
Grid convergence index (GCI). A quantitative estimator of numerical uncertainty attributable to spatial discretisation
error, computed from a monotonic sequence of solutions on systematically refined grids under an assumed observed
order of accuracy. Reported as a percentage band on a selected integrated quantity of interest. The GCI is defined
for solutions that converge to a unique grid-independent limit as the mesh is refined.
Plume resolution index (D*/dx). The ratio of the characteristic plume diameter D* to the representative fire-region
cell edge length dx. D* is the buoyancy-driven length scale associated with a fire heat release rate Q_dot and is
defined as
D* = ( Q_dot / ( rho_inf · cp · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^{2/5}
where rho_inf, cp and T_inf are the ambient density, specific heat and absolute temperature respectively, and g is
gravitational acceleration. The index D*/dx is the standard measure of how many cells span the buoyancy-dominated
length scale of a fire plume.
Resolved turbulent kinetic energy (k_res). The turbulent kinetic energy carried by the explicitly resolved velocity
fluctuations in a large-eddy simulation, distinct from the sub-grid-scale contribution k_sgs modelled by the closure.
The resolved fraction is defined as k_res / (k_res + k_sgs).
RANS and steady work. In this document, "RANS and steady work" means Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes
simulations run to steady state, whether solved with a pseudo-time or true-steady solver, including internal buoyant
airflow of the type in the Copperline municipal HVAC envelope. Unsteady RANS (URANS) is treated as RANS for the
purposes of Section 4.
LES. Large-eddy simulation, including the firm's reacting-fire LES stack (fireFoam with EDC combustion and fvDOM
radiation) and any non-reacting LES of atmospheric or building flow.
3. General Requirements for Verification
Every deliverable that reports a CFD result shall contain a Verification section, plainly labelled as such, appearing in
the body of the report ahead of Validation and ahead of Results. The Verification section shall state, at minimum:
, current revision, or the Units and Conversions SOP
(Firm/Standards/CFDME_Units_SOP_rev2). Where the requirements of this standard intersect those documents, all of them


--- page 2 ---
(a) The turbulence treatment used (RANS, URANS, or LES) and, for LES, the sub-grid-scale closure.
(b) The representative cell edge length dx in the region of interest, and the total cell count.
(c) The verification basis chosen from Section 4 or Section 5, together with the numerical evidence supporting that
basis.
(d) A single-sentence statement identifying which acceptance criterion has been met and by what margin.
The Verification section shall not be an appendix pointer. Numerical values that support the verification claim shall
appear in the body. Supporting figures, residual histories, and mesh-slice imagery may be relegated to an appendix
and referenced.
Verification is prerequisite to Validation. A deliverable whose Verification section is absent, incomplete, or
inconsistent with this standard shall not be released for client transmission and shall not carry a Reviewing Engineer
signature.
4. Grid Convergence Index (GCI)
The Roache/Richardson grid convergence index is the firm's verification instrument for RANS and steady work only.
GCI is not valid for LES and shall not be used to verify any large-eddy result issued from this firm.
The reason is physical. Under systematic mesh refinement, an LES does not converge to a unique grid-independent
solution. As the filter width narrows, energy migrates from the modelled sub-grid-scale contribution into the explicitly
resolved field; the resolved-to-modelled turbulence split changes with the mesh. A three-grid sequence of LES
solutions therefore records a change in the physical content of the simulation between grids rather than a
discretisation-error tail collapsing toward a limit. The Richardson extrapolation on which the GCI is built assumes that
limit exists. It does not exist for LES, and therefore GCI values computed from an LES three-grid study are
numerically well-formed but physically meaningless. Non-monotonic behaviour in an LES three-grid quantity of
interest is the expected signature of the changing split, not evidence of a defective mesh study.
For RANS and steady solves, the firm applies the standard Richardson formulation. Given three systematically
refined grids with representative cell sizes h_1 < h_2 < h_3, refinement ratios r_21 = h_2 / h_1 and r_32 = h_3 / h_2
each at least 1.3, and a scalar quantity of interest phi with values phi_1, phi_2, phi_3 on the three grids, the observed
order of accuracy p is obtained from
phi_3 − phi_2 = ( r_32^p − 1 ) / ( r_21^p − 1 ) · ( phi_2 − phi_1 )
solved for p by fixed-point iteration. The fine-grid GCI on the finest pair is then
GCI_fine = F_s · | ( phi_2 − phi_1 ) / phi_1 | / ( r_21^p − 1 )
with a safety factor F_s of 1.25 when three or more grids are used. Reported GCI values shall carry the safety factor
and the observed p, and shall state the quantity of interest to which they apply. Monotonic convergence is a
precondition for reporting a GCI; oscillatory or divergent triples shall be flagged and the mesh study extended rather
than reported as a GCI band.
The requirement in this Section 4 applies without exception in the RANS envelope. Verification of a steady RANS
solve without a reported GCI (or an equivalent Roache/Richardson estimator) is not accepted.
5. LES Resolution Acceptance
For large-eddy simulations, the firm accepts either of the following as sufficient evidence that the resolution is
adequate in the fire or plume region of interest. Both are preferred; either alone is acceptable.
5.1 Plume resolution index. The plume resolution index D*/dx, computed with D* from the definition in Section 2 and
dx taken as the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region, shall fall in the band 5 to 10.
Values below 5 are insufficient to carry the buoyancy-driven length scale; values above 10 are wasteful of compute
without corresponding gain in fidelity for the classes of fires the firm simulates. Q_dot in the D* expression is the fire
heat release rate applied in the LES, in watts.
5.2 Pope resolved-TKE criterion. The resolved turbulent kinetic energy shall be at least 80% of the total turbulent
kinetic energy in the region of interest, i.e.
k_res / ( k_res + k_sgs ) >= 0.8


--- page 3 ---
This is Pope's criterion for a well-resolved LES. The ratio shall be computed on a time-average of a statistically
converged solution window (typically ten or more integral time scales, or ten or more puffing cycles for a pool-fire-like
plume). Point probes shall be located within the buoyancy-dominated flow, not on the periphery of the domain.
Either criterion, met, is acceptable. Meeting both is preferred and is the default expectation for deliverables prepared
for authorities-having-jurisdiction or life-safety end use. Neither criterion may be evaded by asserting engineering
judgement in place of the numerical evidence; where a physical constraint prevents meeting either criterion, the
constraint and its consequence shall be stated explicitly in the Verification section and the deliverable escalated to
the Reviewing Engineer before release.
6. Reporting
The Verification section of every LES deliverable shall state, directly in the body of the report:
•
The fire heat release rate Q_dot used to compute D*, with units.
•
The characteristic plume diameter D*, with units.
•
The representative cell edge length dx in the region of interest, with units.
•
The plume resolution index D*/dx as a dimensionless number.
•
The Pope resolved-TKE fraction k_res / (k_res + k_sgs) as a percentage, together with the location of the probe(s)
and the length of the averaging window.
These values shall appear in the running text or in a table in the Verification section itself. Placement of any of these
values in an appendix, with only a cross-reference in the Verification section, does not satisfy this standard.
GCI values shall not appear in LES deliverables. A three-grid table copied forward from a RANS template into an
LES report, whether or not it is accompanied by a GCI band, is a non-compliant Verification section under this
standard. If a three-grid mesh study has been carried out on an LES case for information (for example, to
demonstrate insensitivity of an integrated quantity), the tabulated values may be included in an appendix labelled as
a sensitivity study, but they shall not be presented as verification evidence and no GCI shall be computed from them.
The Verification section of a RANS or steady deliverable shall state the observed order of accuracy p, the fine-grid
GCI on the reported quantity of interest with its safety factor, and the refinement ratios. D*/dx and Pope's criterion do
not apply to RANS deliverables and shall not be reported there.
7. Roles
Project Engineer. Responsible for constructing the mesh study or resolution assessment appropriate to the
turbulence treatment, computing the required indices, and drafting the Verification section in accordance with
Sections 3, 4, 5 and 6.
Reviewing Engineer. Responsible for confirming, on the peer-review checklist, that the Verification section of the
deliverable meets the requirements of this standard. The confirmation is a specific line item on the checklist and shall
not be a general "verification section reviewed" tick. For an LES deliverable, the Reviewing Engineer shall confirm
that D*, dx, D*/dx, and the Pope resolved-TKE fraction appear in the body of the report and that no GCI value has
been carried forward from a RANS template. For a RANS or steady deliverable, the Reviewing Engineer shall confirm
the presence of the observed order p, the GCI band and its safety factor, and monotonic convergence of the
underlying triple.
Owner / Principal Engineer. Retains final responsibility for the stamped CFD thermal analysis and for any release of
a deliverable in which the Reviewing Engineer has flagged a Verification-section deficiency that has not been
resolved.
8. References

10 [Normal] 1. Purpose & Scope
11 [Normal] 1.1 Purpose
12 [Normal] This report documents the Phase 1 thermal-CFD analysis of the Ocotillo Additive Structures double-wythe printed-concrete cavity wall assembly under Sonoran Desert wildland-urban-interface exposure. The analysis is a large-eddy simulation of a fire-front segment representative of a Sonoran buffelgrass surface fire advancing on the exposed face of the assembly. The exposure envelope, fire-source characterisation, mesh study, and preliminary thermal response are reported here. Companion structural wind-pressure work under SOW Section 3.2 is documented separately.
13 [Normal] 1.2 Scope
14 [Normal] The scope of the Phase 1 analysis is limited to:
15 [List Bullet] Regime classification and selection of solver stack;
16 [List Bullet] Site-envelope characterisation from Pima County ALERT ten-year hourly meteorology;
17 [List Bullet] Fire-source characterisation from published Rothermel / Byram / solid-flame correlations for the specified fuel model;
18 [List Bullet] Large-eddy simulation of the fire-front sub-domain at design-envelope wind speeds and directions;
19 [List Bullet] Thermal treatment of the double-wythe cavity wall assembly per the project case-setup record;
20 [List Bullet] Verification of the LES discretisation on the wildfire sub-domain;
21 [List Bullet] Preliminary reporting of unexposed-face and tie-embedded thermal response.
22 [Normal] 1.3 Scope exclusions
23 [Normal] Fire-resistance rating certification of the assembly is explicitly outside the scope of this report and outside the stamp boundary of The CFD ME. The certified rating for the subject wall assembly is issued separately by others (see the standard stamp block in §9). This report is a computational thermal analysis; it does not certify, extend, or modify any assembly rating.
24 [Normal] Structural wind-pressure work per SOW §3.2 is a separate deliverable and is not included here.
25 [Normal] 2. Governing SOW Reference
26 [Normal] 2.1 Statement of Work
27 [Normal] The governing contract for the analysis reported here is the Ocotillo Additive Structures Phase 1 Statement of Work, CFDME-2025-041, signed 10/08/2025. Two technical sections of the SOW frame the Phase 1 workscope:
28 [Normal] 2.2 SOW §3.1 — Wildfire Analysis Matrix
29 [Normal] Six wildfire-exposure cases, formed as the cross-product of two wind directions and three wind speeds:
31 [Normal] The two directions bracket the prevailing daytime westerly component observed at the Avra Valley WUI site; the three speeds span the site design 20-ft wind envelope of 5–12 m/s (§5).
32 [Normal] 2.3 SOW §3.2 — Structural Wind-Load Case
33 [Normal] SOW §3.2 defines a separate structural wind-pressure extraction for the wall assembly per ASCE 7-22, sited in Tucson, Arizona, at Exposure C, Risk Category II. That extraction is reported in a separate deliverable and is not carried in this report; the SOW §3.1 wildfire matrix and the SOW §3.2 structural case are distinct workscopes and share no boundary conditions.
34 [Normal] 3. Method
35 [Normal] 3.1 Regime classification
36 [Normal] Regime classification for this matrix follows CFD Modeling Standards — Fire & Buoyant Flows rev 4 (§2), evaluated against the site design 20-ft wind speed envelope of 5–12 m/s and the design fire heat release rate (§3.3). The classification and the resulting solver selection are documented in the project case-setup record (CFDME-2025-041_scoping_memo_20251008.docx §4) and are not re-derived here.
37 [Normal] 3.2 Solver stack
38 [Normal] Solver stack selection for this matrix is governed by the firm modeling standard §3 and is documented in the project case-setup record; that record is the reference for the solver, inlet, combustion, and radiation model selection used to produce the results in §5 below.
39 [Normal] 3.3 Fire source
40 [Normal] The exposed-face heat load is imposed as a sub-domain LES over a 3.0 m segment of the advancing fire front, taken at the point of nearest approach to the assembly. The total heat release rate over that segment is 30.1 MW, sourced by a volumetric heat-release term integrated over the fuel bed footprint within the sub-domain. The Byram fireline intensity and solid-flame flame length that underpin this source term are given in §5.
41 [Normal] 3.4 Wall assembly
42 [Normal] The wall assembly is a double-wythe printed-concrete cavity wall, source of record OAS-WUI-01_revC: two 50 mm printed siliceous-aggregate concrete leaves separated by a 205 mm open-air cavity (no insulation), tied by continuous 9-gauge (3.8 mm) galvanized truss-type steel ties at 600 mm vertical spacing, 25 mm embedment each leaf. Overall assembly thickness is 305 mm. The through-wall CFD treatment selected for this assembly is documented in the project case-setup record per Modeling Standard §6.
43 [Normal] 3.5 Geometry of record
44 [Normal] The source geometry for all cases reported here is OAS-WUI-01_revC, transmitted by the client with the signed SOW on 10/08/2025 and meshed the morning of 10/09/2025. Every case log, mesh output, and results file in this report references OAS-WUI-01_revC as source geometry. The architectural drawing for the same assembly (OAS_wall_assembly_section.png) uses the drawing-side identifier OAS-WA-305mm-DW; this refers to the same physical wall assembly as the engineering geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC used throughout this report.
45 [Normal] 4. Assumptions & Limitations
46 [Normal] 4.1 Assumptions
47 [List Bullet] Fuel model. Sonoran buffelgrass is treated as a continuous, homogeneous surface fuel bed at the fuel load and heat content given in §5. Fuel spatial heterogeneity below the sub-domain footprint is not represented.
48 [List Bullet] Fire-source stationarity. The 3.0 m front segment is held stationary within the LES sub-domain; the wall assembly is at the point of nearest approach for the sampled interval. Fire-front advance across the assembly footprint is not simulated within the sub-domain.
49 [List Bullet] Meteorological stationarity. Inlet wind speed and direction are stationary within each case at the values in the SOW §3.1 matrix; diurnal, gust, and synoptic-scale variability are represented only by the envelope in §5.
50 [List Bullet] Cavity contents. The cavity is modelled as open air with no insulation, per the as-built assembly.
51 [List Bullet] Concrete properties. Printed siliceous-aggregate concrete properties are those in the modeling standard reference table, with temperature dependence enabled; spatial variability introduced by the printing process is not represented.
52 [List Bullet] Radiation participation. Concrete surfaces are treated as grey diffuse emitters at emissivity 0.9, per the radiation model selected in the project case-setup record.
53 [Normal] 4.2 Limitations
54 [List Bullet] The analysis is a thermal analysis only. It does not certify fire-resistance rating, does not predict structural collapse, and does not predict spalling.
55 [List Bullet] The analysis reports response to the SOW §3.1 wildfire matrix. It does not predict survival of the assembly under exposures outside that envelope.
56 [List Bullet] The ASTM E119 furnace exposure is a comparative-rating exposure; a companion E119 simulation is reported under Validation (§7) for model-verification purposes only. E119 endurance is not a wildfire survival prediction.
57 [List Bullet] Validation of the wildfire configuration against a wildfire-phase physical test is scheduled for the Red Butte confirmatory window on 10/27/2025 and is not reported here.
58 [Normal] 5. Results
59 [Normal] 5.1 Site design envelope
60 [Normal] Ten-year hourly meteorology from the Pima County ALERT network at the Avra Valley WUI site establishes the design exposure envelope:
62 [Normal] These ranges bracket the fire-season daytime conditions used for the SOW §3.1 matrix inlets.
63 [Normal] 5.2 Fire-source characterisation
64 [Normal] For the Sonoran buffelgrass fuel model at the site design envelope:
66 [Normal] The 5.4 m solid-flame length is the wind-tilted Byram length. It is shorter than the still-air Heskestad correlation at 30.1 MW / 3.0 m (which would predict ~11.5 m); this gap between the two correlations is not treated as a discrepancy.
67 [Normal] 5.3 Plume dynamics
68 [Normal] The plume in every solved case exhibits a well-organised puffing signature at the plume base, with a puffing frequency of 0.87 Hz. The puffing signature is resolved in time by the transient LES; centreline temperature and velocity monitors oscillate at that frequency about their mean values, sampled over no fewer than twenty puffing cycles at t ≥ 8 s.
69 [Normal] 5.4 Thermal response — preliminary
70 [Normal] Preliminary plume-centreline peaks on the fine grid are T_peak ≈ 1461 K and U_z,peak ≈ 12.4 m/s at the reference probe location (0.75·D* above the source top surface). Per-case unexposed-face and tie-embedded temperature histories for the six SOW §3.1 cases will be reported in Appendix B upon completion of the production LES runs (scheduled Sprint 2, 2025-10-20).
71 [Normal] 6. Verification
72 [Normal] 6.1 Three-grid study
73 [Normal] A three-grid study was executed on the wildfire sub-domain over the OAS-WUI-01_revC geometry, following the firm's verification reporting layout. Background cell sizes and headline monitors on the plume centreline at t = 40.0 s are:
75 [Normal] Every mesh passes the firm mesh-quality criteria (max non-orthogonality, max skewness, max aspect ratio) with "Mesh OK." returned by checkMesh on every grid. Transient time stepping per firm standard §4 applies to all three runs; puffing period is recovered on all three grids.
76 [Normal] 6.2 Grid-to-grid comparison
77 [Normal] Grid-to-grid behaviour of the T_peak and U_z,peak monitors is non-monotonic across the three grids. The corresponding puffing-period monitor is essentially converged from the medium grid onward. The fire-source refinement zone carries two additional refinement levels above background on every grid; the ratio of refined-zone cell size to background cell size is preserved across the three cases.
78 [Normal] 6.3 Selection of reporting grid
79 [Normal] The fine grid (background dx = 0.5 m) is retained as the reporting grid for the six SOW §3.1 wildfire cases. Detail of the underlying LES resolution figures on that grid is given in Appendix C.
80 [Normal] 7. Validation
81 [Normal] (To be completed. Companion simulation predicts S = 131 min for the ASTM E119 exposure; validation memo forthcoming.)
82 [Normal] 8. Conclusions
83 [Normal] (Placeholder — to be written pending completion of §7 and the confirmatory Red Butte window on 10/27/2025.)

99 [Normal] Boundary-condition summary for each of the six SOW §3.1 wildfire cases (240°/270° × 5, 8, 12 m/s at 20 ft), including wind-inlet reference height, roughness length, ambient temperature, and relative humidity from the site envelope in §5.1.

0 [Normal] THE CFD ME   |   Tucson, Arizona   |   AZ PE #48213   |   CFDME-2025-041 rev A
5 [Normal] MEMORANDUM — PHASE 1 SCOPING
7 [Normal] 1.  Purpose & Scope
8 [Normal] This memo fixes, at project kickoff and before any meshing is undertaken, the first-principles basis on which the Phase 1 wildfire-exposure large-eddy simulation set will be built. It records the design conditions taken from the site meteorological pull, the buffelgrass fuel model, the Rothermel-to-Byram source-term chain that produces the design fire, the Froude regime assessment inputs, and the LES sub-domain geometry against which downstream mesh sizing will be measured. It is issued on the effective date of the Ocotillo Additive Structures Phase 1 Statement of Work (CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01, signed 10/08/2025), before revC of the assembly geometry (OAS-WUI-01_revC, transmitted with the SOW) is imported into the mesher.
9 [Normal] The intent is that every downstream case-setup artifact, mesh-study artifact, and Phase 1 reporting deliverable — including the interim hand-calc due 10/13/2025 and the LES setup deliverable due 10/20/2025 — trace their source-term, regime, and geometry inputs back to the numbers recorded here, rather than re-argue them case-by-case. Where a downstream artifact needs the design fire heat release, the characteristic source diameter, or the plume length scale, it shall cite this memo.
10 [Normal] The scope of Phase 1 as procured under Section 3.1 of the SOW is six transient wildfire cases (240 deg and 270 deg wind directions at 20-ft wind speeds of 5, 8, and 12 m/s). The fire source term and the sub-domain sizing recorded here apply to that entire matrix; they are not per-case parameters.
11 [Normal] 2.  Site Design Conditions
12 [Normal] Design conditions are taken from the ten-year hourly record of the Pima County ALERT network for the Avra Valley WUI corridor west of Tucson (data pull: site_met_avra_valley_2015-2024.csv, Section 3.1 of the SOW envelope). The following envelope governs Phase 1:
14 [Normal] These conditions define the site for regime classification (Section 4 below) and for the source-term chain (Section 3 below). They are the same conditions carried into the Phase 1 report; no re-derivation is required.
15 [Normal] 3.  Fuel Model — Sonoran Buffelgrass at Site Design Conditions
16 [Normal] The design fire source term is developed under the Rothermel spread-to-Byram intensity chain, evaluated at the site design conditions of Section 2. The buffelgrass fuel model is adopted per the SOW Section 2 definition (“Buffelgrass Fuel Model”). Fuel-model quantities are:
17 [Normal] •  Fuel load (dry):  w = 0.6 kg/m²
18 [Normal] •  Low heat of combustion:  h = 18,600 kJ/kg
19 [Normal] •  Rate of spread at design wind:  R = 0.9 m/s
20 [Normal] R is the head-fire rate of spread produced by the Rothermel surface-fire spread model for cured buffelgrass at the low-humidity, high-temperature, moderate-wind conditions of Section 2. It is used here as the input to the Byram fireline-intensity relation; the Rothermel-model input parameter tabulation for buffelgrass is on file with the project data pull.
21 [Normal] Byram’s fireline intensity is the product of the low heat of combustion, the available fuel load per unit area, and the rate of spread:
22 [Normal] I = h · w · R
23 [Normal]   = (18,600 kJ/kg) × (0.6 kg/m²) × (0.9 m/s)
24 [Normal]   = 10,040 kW/m
25 [Normal] The Byram wind-tilted solid-flame length correlation gives:
26 [Normal] L = 0.0775 · I^0.46
27 [Normal]   = 0.0775 × (10,040)^0.46
28 [Normal]   = 5.4 m
29 [Normal] L above is the wind-tilted Byram flame length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height and is not comparable to Heskestad’s still-air correlation (see Section 5 for the idealization record).
30 [Normal] 4.  Froude / Regime Assessment
31 [Normal] Regime selection follows CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §2. The controlling non-dimensional group is the Froude number formed on the characteristic source diameter of the LES sub-domain:
32 [Normal] Fr = u_wind / sqrt(g · D_char)
33 [Normal] Taking D_char = 3.0 m (the LES sub-domain segment fixed in Section 5 below) and g = 9.81 m/s²:
34 [Normal] sqrt(g · D_char) = sqrt(9.81 × 3.0) = sqrt(29.43) = 5.42 m/s
35 [Normal] Evaluated across the site design wind envelope 5–12 m/s:
37 [Normal] The Froude / plume-velocity ratio falls in the range ~0.9–2.2 across the entire design envelope.
38 [Normal] Regime classification.  Classification against the Modeling Standard §2 thresholds, and solver selection per §3 of that standard, shall be carried out and documented in the case setup record before any case in this matrix is meshed.
39 [Normal] This classification is made once, at the firm level, for the entire Phase 1 wildfire matrix; it is not re-argued case-by-case within the envelope.
40 [Normal] 5.  LES Sub-Domain
41 [Normal] The LES sub-domain represents a 3.0 m segment of the flaming front. This segment length is the characteristic source width used for the plume model, and the value of D_char used in the Section 4 Froude computation and in the plume-length-scale computation below.
42 [Normal] 5.1  Line vs Axisymmetric Reconciliation
43 [Normal] The Byram fireline-intensity relation of Section 3 gives an intensity per unit length of the fire front (kW/m). The plume length scale D* referred to by the firm modeling and verification standards is an axisymmetric-source property (kW total). The two quantities are not interchangeable and cannot be composed directly. The 3.0 m segment length is the specific conversion factor between them for this project: it defines how much fire-front length is captured within one LES sub-domain, and therefore what total heat release rate the plume model sees.
44 [Normal] Design fire heat release rate for the sub-domain:
45 [Normal] Q = I × L_segment
46 [Normal]   = (10,040 kW/m) × (3.0 m)
47 [Normal]   = 30,120 kW
48 [Normal]   = 30.1 MW
49 [Normal] Idealizations recorded so they are not misread as physical dimensions.
50 [Normal] •  Flame depth and flame residence time are not resolved in this sub-domain. The flaming front is represented as an equivalent 3.0 m characteristic-diameter source patch.
51 [Normal] •  The wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m from Section 3 is a wind-tilted correlation length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height. Heskestad’s still-air flame-height correlation, evaluated for the same 30.1 MW heat release rate at a 3.0 m diameter source, gives roughly 11.5 m. The 5.4 m vs 11.5 m gap between the two correlations is not treated as a discrepancy between two attempts to model the same quantity.
52 [Normal] Plume characteristic diameter D*.  For Q = 30.1 MW and standard reference-atmosphere conditions (ρ_∞ = 1.204 kg/m³, c_p = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, T_∞ = 293.15 K, g = 9.81 m/s²):
53 [Normal] D* = ( Q / ( rho_inf · c_p · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^(2/5)
54 [Normal]    = ( 30,100 / ( 1.204 × 1.005 × 293.15 × 3.132 ) )^(2/5)
55 [Normal]    = ( 27.08 )^(2/5)
56 [Normal] D* = 3.76 m.
57 [Normal] The fine-grid cell size specified for the LES mesh study is dx = 0.5 m (the finest of the three grids in the mesh study). This gives:
58 [Normal] D* / dx = 3.76 / 0.5 = 7.5
59 [Normal] which confirms the plume is adequately resolved on the fine grid. LES resolution acceptance shall be assessed per the firm QA standard applicable to reacting-plume LES.
60 [Normal] 6.  Wall Assembly Note
61 [Normal] The through-wall response of the assembly cannot be modelled as heat conduction through a single solid slab. Per the OAS-WUI-01_revC wall assembly section (Geometry/OAS_wall_assembly_section.png), the assembly is a double-wythe cavity system: two 50 mm printed-concrete leaves separated by a 205 mm open-air cavity (overall thickness 305 mm), tied together by continuous 9-gauge (3.8 mm) galvanized truss-type steel ties spaced 600 mm on centre vertically, embedded 25 mm into each leaf. The cavity carries no insulation. The architectural drawing (OAS_wall_assembly_section.png) uses the drawing-side identifier OAS-WA-305mm-DW in its title block; this refers to the same physical wall assembly as the engineering geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC used throughout the SOW, this memo, and all downstream analysis artifacts.
62 [Normal] The metallic ties are a continuous parallel thermal path between the exposed and unexposed leaves; their conductivity (~45 W/m·K) is more than an order of magnitude above the siliceous-aggregate concrete of the leaves, and they are the reason the single-point criterion governs over the average-rise criterion in the ASTM E119 test result of record.
63 [Normal] Per CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §6, the through-wall modeling treatment for this assembly shall be selected and documented in the case setup record before meshing, accounting for the metallic ties’ thermal-bridge role identified above. Temperature-dependent solid properties (k, ρ, c_p) apply per Modeling Standard §3.5.
64 [Normal] 7.  Downstream Inputs
65 [Normal] The following quantities established above are the source-term and length-scale inputs for the downstream Phase 1 case-setup, mesh-study, and reporting artifacts:
66 [Normal] •  Site design envelope: ambient 35–42 °C, RH 10–25 %, 20-ft wind 5–12 m/s (Section 2).
67 [Normal] •  Byram fireline intensity I = 10,040 kW/m (Section 3).
68 [Normal] •  Wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m (Section 3).
69 [Normal] •  LES sub-domain fire-front segment: 3.0 m (Section 5).
70 [Normal] •  Design fire heat release rate: 30.1 MW (Section 5.1).
71 [Normal] •  Plume characteristic diameter: D* = 3.76 m (Section 5.1).
72 [Normal] •  Froude ratio range across the site design envelope: ~0.9–2.2 (Section 4); regime classification and solver selection per Modeling Standard §§2–3 to be documented in the case setup record (Section 4).
73 [Normal] •  Wall through-thickness modeling treatment: to be selected and documented per Modeling Standard §6, accounting for the metallic tie thermal-bridge path identified in Section 6.
74 [Normal] The 3.0 m segment, 30.1 MW source, and D* = 3.76 m established per Section 5 above are the inputs the fine grid dx = 0.5 m recorded in the Meshing and case-build log is sized against.
75 [Normal] The 5–12 m/s design wind envelope carries forward into the wind-inlet boundary conditions of the six-case matrix, per the solver selection made in Section 4; the puffing frequency of 0.87 Hz predicted by the f = 1.5·D^(-1/2) correlation per CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §4 for this plume sets the writeInterval and end-time requirements for each transient run.

Section 3.2 asks the firm to develop the code-basis wall pressures at the OAS-WUI-01 envelope for a discrete-wind-speed check independent of the wildfire matrix, and to report peak pressures on windward, side, and leeward faces at probe locations laid out in the case verification plan. The values summarized below are drawn directly from the interim probe extraction (interim_wall_pressures.csv, 10/09/2025) with no post-processing beyond the peak rollup.
2. Case Description
Basis of loading: ASCE 7-22 (Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures).
Site: Tucson, Arizona (Ocotillo pilot envelope, OAS-WUI-01_revC geometry of record).

The probe grid used for peak extraction consists of ten windward probes spanning the windward face, five probes on each side wall (north and south), and five probes on the leeward face. Probe elevations are 0.8 m, 3.2 m, and 5.6 m above grade. All probe values reported are peak (envelope) values from the interim extraction.

Windward wall | 12.4 Pa | WW_02, WW_03, WW_04, WW_06, WW_07, WW_08
Side wall (peak suction) | −9.5 Pa | SW_S_01
Leeward wall (peak suction) | −6.1 Pa | LW_01, LW_03

Sign convention: positive pressures act inward on the wall face; negative pressures indicate suction (outward). Values are peaks across the interim probe set; the full per-probe listing is retained in interim_wall_pressures.csv.
4. Discussion
Taken at face value, the pressures returned by the interim rollup are negligible relative to the structural design demand envelope typically associated with the framing of a 6.4 m mean-roof-height enclosed building at a 96 mph basic wind speed in Exposure C. A 12.4 Pa peak windward pressure is a very small fraction of the wall loads that would ordinarily drive sizing of tie, header, and out-of-plane bending checks for a printed-concrete assembly of this scale, and the corresponding side-wall and leeward suctions (−9.5 Pa and −6.1 Pa peak) are similarly small.
On that basis the interim reading is that the ASCE 7-22 wall loading, taken as extracted, does not govern the OAS-WUI-01 envelope. Wildfire-driven radiative and convective loading (SOW Section 3.1) and the E119 fire-endurance envelope remain the controlling design considerations for the assembly. No structural remediation of the OAS-WUI-01_revC envelope is indicated by this interim result.
The client should treat these figures as provisional pending peer review under the firm's QA workflow. The values here are unchanged from the interim rollup and have not been checked against boundary-condition inputs or reconciled with the ASCE 7-22 velocity-pressure and pressure-coefficient hand calculation feeding the extraction; those cross-checks are open items on the peer-review checklist and will be addressed before the Phase 1 structural wind-load memo is issued.

1. Purpose and Background
Client designs and constructs single-family residential structures using proprietary additive-manufactured (3D-printed)

interface ("WUI") of the Sonoran Desert west of Tucson, Arizona. Client's marketing programme advances the
positioning that Client's printed-concrete envelope is more fire-resistant, under credible wildfire exposure, than
conventional wood-frame construction of comparable footprint.
Consultant is engaged to provide the computational-fluid-dynamics ("CFD") backing for that positioning as it applies
to a Sonoran Desert buffelgrass wildfire event in the Avra Valley WUI corridor west of Tucson. The engagement
covers Phase 1 only: the mixed-convection wildfire plume analyses enumerated in Section 3.1 and the structural
wind-pressure extraction enumerated in Section 3.2, together with the deliverables in Section 4.
Client acknowledges that fire-resistance ratings on the printed wall assembly (including the current 1-hour rating
already issued by others) are outside the scope of this SOW and are certified separately by a third-party
fire-protection engineer under a separate engagement. This SOW procures analysis only.
2. Definitions
For purposes of this SOW, the following terms have the meanings given below.
"Assembly" — the double-wythe printed-concrete wall system, geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC as
transmitted by Client to Consultant on the Effective Date.
"Buffelgrass Fuel Model" — the Sonoran-desert buffelgrass ground-fuel model adopted for the wildfire source term
in the Section 3.1 matrix, as documented in Consultant's Phase 1 scoping memo of even date.
"LES" — large-eddy simulation, meaning transient turbulence-resolving CFD run with wall time-step control per
Consultant's internal modelling standard for reacting buoyant flows.
"Site" — the Avra Valley Sonoran Desert WUI parcel west of Tucson identified in Client's Phase 0 site file.
"Wildfire Matrix" — the six-case matrix of atmospheric conditions and wind directions defined in Section 3.1.
"Structural Wind Case" — the single ASCE 7-22 wind-pressure load case defined in Section 3.2.
"Change Order" — a written amendment to this SOW, executed by both parties, before performance, that modifies
scope, schedule, or fee.

load cases with separate governing bases; results from one shall not be substituted for or compared against results
from the other.

1. Purpose
This memo documents validation of the Dry Wash high-altitude external aerodynamics case (CFDME-2024-018)
against the wind-tunnel measurements of record for the airframe geometry and freestream conditions covered by the
Dry Wash SOW. It records the comparison of computed and measured surface pressure coefficients across the
operating envelope, states the envelope in which the case is validated, and states the conditions under which that
status does not transfer.
The output of this memo is a validated status attached to a specific case within a specifically bounded envelope. It is
not a certification of the geometry, the solver, or any directory containing the case files. Reuse outside the stated
envelope requires re-validation per firm modeling standards.
2. Case Description
The validated case is archived at:
CFDME-2024-018/Case/DWA_highaltitude_case_setup.txt
Salient features of the case, restated from the archive:
•
Solver: rhoSimpleFoam — steady-state, pressure-based, compressible.
•
Chemistry / reactions: none. The case is compressible non-reacting. No reactive scalar transport is compiled
into the solve, and there is no combustion model.

Radiation: off. The constant/ directory carries no radiationProperties dictionary and no radiative source

Turbulence: RAS, k-omega SST, wall-function resolved (kqRWallFunction / omegaWallFunction /

required within the validated envelope.
•
Freestream: high-altitude flight conditions — reference pressure 26,500 Pa, reference temperature 223 K,
freestream density 0.4 kg/m3 at altitude, Mach 0.25, fully turbulent Reynolds regime.
•
Boundary conditions: airframe treated as adiabatic no-slip wall; farfield freestream on the outer boundary. No
conjugate heat-transfer regions, no cavity or multi-region entries.

Time stepping: steady-state (ddtSchemes default steadyState, adjustTimeStep no, endTime in

The case as archived matches, without modification, the case that produced the computed pressure coefficients

coefficient (Cp) taps distributed across the body at stations covering the operating envelope; both freestream Mach

The reference dataset carries pressure coefficients only. It does not contain:

surface or gas temperature measurements,

heat flux measurements,

any reacting-flow scalar (species mass fractions, heat-release rate, radiant intensity),

# Asks in the instruction and direct answers (mirrors note sections)

## A1. Where does the plume resolution index land for the result the report rests on — with cell size and plume length scale, and is our band met?
**Answer:** The fine grid retained for the six SOW §3.1 cases (report rev B §6.3) is at **D*/dx = 29.9 (dimensionless)**, or **30.1** using the report's rounded D* = 3.76 m — not 7.5. The recomputed plume length scale is **D* = 3.74 m** for Q = 30.1 MW with the report ambient (rho = 1.204 kg/m3, cp = 1005 J/(kg K), T = 293.15 K). The representative fire-region cell is **dx = 0.125 m** (two snappy refinement levels below the 0.5 m background; level 5 within 3.00 m of the plumeSource), not the 0.5 m background cell. The firm band 5 to 10 is **NOT MET**, on the high side: the fire region is about 3x over-resolved (upper-bound utilisation 2.99). The report's 7.5 is 3.76/0.5, i.e. correct only for the background cell. Source: QA VS rev 3 §5.1; report rev B §6.2/§6.3/Appendix C; log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt; scoping memo §5.1.

## A2. What does our resolution acceptance rest on?
**Answer:** Governing basis is QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5: either D*/dx in 5–10 (§5.1) or Pope k_res/(k_res+k_sgs) >= 0.8 on a >=10-cycle time average with probes in the buoyancy-dominated flow (§5.2); either alone is acceptable, both preferred. Section 6 requires Q, D*, dx, D*/dx, Pope fraction, probe location and averaging window in the Verification body, prohibits GCI in LES deliverables, and allows a three-grid table only as an appendix sensitivity study. The project record currently rests on (a) the scoping memo 10/08/2025 value 7.5 computed on the 0.5 m background cell and (b) a three-grid table in report §6.1. Neither is valid LES verification: GCI assumes a unique grid-independent limit that LES does not have, and the table is non-monotonic (T_peak 1420/1487/1461 K; U_z 12.8/11.2/12.4 m/s). The only possible alternative is the 84% Pope figure, but it is not traceable (no k_res/k_sgs, no probe record, no averaging start/end or sample count; the only solver log on file is a steady RANS attempt, not LES). If attempt 3 is the run of record, QA VS §4 applies instead and requires a RANS GCI (observed p, refinement ratios and Fs = 1.25), which is also absent.

## A3. Does anything about that basis need a decision from Marguerite?
**Answer:** Yes, two decisions as Reviewing Engineer and author of record of QA VS rev 3:
1. Whether D*/dx = 29.9 on the 0.125 m fire-region cell (above the band's upper bound of 10) is accepted as documented over-resolution under §5.1 — QA VS calls >10 "wasteful of compute", not inadequate — or treated as a nonconformance requiring revision. This also confirms the dx reading: if §5.1 were read as allowing the 0.5 m background, the index would be 7.5 and the band would appear met.
2. Whether the existing 84% Pope record is sufficient to carry acceptance on the Pope criterion alone under §5.2, or must be reproduced from traceable LES output. If either answer is no, item 4 stays open. Marguerite also signed the 10/08/2025 scoping memo that fixed 7.5 on the 0.5 m background; the stricter QA reading (0.125 m fire-region cell) supersedes that dx value.

## A4. Was the resolved-energy figure taken inside the region the index describes?
**Answer:** Nominally yes. The 84% is at the plume-centreline probe 0.75·D* above the source top (2.81 m for D* = 3.74 m), on the plume axis inside the 3.00 m level-5 refined zone and the buoyancy-dominated flow — not a domain average. But it is a single point with no k_res/k_sgs values, no averaging start/end or sample count, and no probe record in the solve log (probes are at z = 4, 8 and 12 m AGL, not 2.8 m). So the location is acceptable in principle but the figure is not demonstrated by the record.

## A5. Do the ambient values behind D* represent the site, and what would site conditions do to it?
**Answer:** No. The reported D* uses rho = 1.204 kg/m3 and T = 293.15 K (sea-level 20 °C), while the site design envelope is 35–42 °C, 10–25% RH, 5–12 m/s at 20 ft at ~750 m elevation (wind-load basis memo §2.1a). At 750 m ISA pressure is 92.6 kPa; with consistent density, D* = 3.88 m (+3.7%) and D*/dx = 31.0 at dx = 0.125 m. Temperature alone cancels at fixed pressure; holding rho = 1.204 and heating to 42 °C gives D* = 3.64 m and D*/dx = 29.1, still outside the band. Site conditions do not fix the band. ## A6. Can checklist item 4 close, and if not, what would settle it?
**Answer:** It **cannot close on the present record**. Reasons: actual D*/dx is 29.9–30.1, not in the 5–10 band; the only alternative is the 84% Pope figure, which is not supported by a traceable LES calculation in the Verification body; and the resolution values are in Appendix C while a three-grid table is presented as verification in §6.1, contrary to QA VS rev 3 §6. 1. Scope and General Principles
This procedure governs the units in which engineering quantities are computed, recorded, exchanged, and reported
at The CFD ME. It applies to every analyst and reviewer inside the firm, to every contracted CFD hour executed by
third parties on our behalf, and to every artifact — case files, logs, hand-calc worksheets, memos, and client

The governing principles are three:
SI units shall be used internally throughout all analyses. Reports transmitted to clients working in US customary units
shall include a conversion table in report Section 1. Every numeric value in every artifact shall carry its unit in the
same cell or sentence — a bare number without unit is a defect.

satisfied by keeping the analysis in SI from mesh generation through post-processing so that reviewers see a single
coherent unit system when they audit a case. The conversion table is not optional decoration; on projects whose

inherited from a section heading.

Column headers in CSV and TXT deliverables shall carry the unit in the header string (e.g., T_unexposed_max_C,
pressure_Pa, time_min). Plot axes shall carry the unit in the axis label. Memos and report body prose shall carry
the unit adjacent to every numeric value.
3. Conversions in Routine Use
The following conversions arise routinely in this office's work — ASCE 7-22 wind-load extraction, ASHRAE HVAC
inputs, ASTM E119 lab reports, and construction-industry submittals. The values below are the firm-blessed
conversion factors and shall be used verbatim; do not re-derive from memory at the desk.
•
1 psf = 47.88 Pa
•
1 psi = 6895 Pa
•
1 lb (force) = 4.448 N
•
1 in = 25.4 mm
•
1 ft = 0.3048 m
•
1 BTU/hr·ft² = 3.155 W/m²
•
1 K = 1 °C (for temperature differences only; not for absolute temperatures)
•
T[K] = T[°C] + 273.15 (for absolute temperature conversion)
Two of the above deserve emphasis. First, the psf-to-Pa factor is 47.88, not unity — a psf value carried into a Pa field
without applying the factor is off by nearly two orders of magnitude, which is precisely the failure mode this SOP
exists to prevent. Second, the temperature-difference identity (1 K = 1 °C) applies only to differences; a rise of 139 °C
is a rise of 139 K, but an absolute temperature of 139 °C is 412.15 K, not 139 K.
Additional conversions not listed above shall be sourced from the NIST SP 811 tables and cited by page in the
analyst's worksheet. Conversion factors quoted from web calculators, textbook back-covers, or LLM outputs shall not
be used.
4. Sanity Check Requirement


--- page 3 ---
Every reported field value shall be sanity-checked against the governing boundary conditions of the load case it
belongs to before rollup. Reviewers shall confirm this check on the peer-review checklist (item 9). A pressure reported
at a scale inconsistent with the case boundary conditions is a defect regardless of unit label.
The check is a scale check, not a unit check. A pressure field whose header reads "Pa" but whose values sit at a
magnitude the boundary conditions cannot produce is defective even if the string "Pa" is technically the intended unit;
the label alone does not vindicate the number. The check is performed at three points in the workflow: (a) by the
case-setup engineer immediately after the first converged or first fully-transient output is produced, (b) by the rollup
engineer at the moment values move from raw fields into summary tables, and (c) by the reviewer at peer review. The
reviewer's confirmation is recorded against item 9 of the peer-review checklist for that project.
Sanity checks are performed against the boundary conditions of the same load case. Cross-case checks are
governed separately by Section 5.
5. Cross-Case Cross-Checks
reported from one case shall not be checked against the boundary conditions of the other.
and their pressure fields are stored in the same case-folder hierarchy. A reviewer who reaches for the wildfire
boundary conditions when sanity-checking a structural wind pressure — or vice versa — will incorrectly clear values
that belong to the other case, or incorrectly flag values that were correct all along. Each case has its own boundary
conditions and its own expected scale, and each is sanity-checked only against its own.
Where a report presents results from both cases, the report body shall separate them under clearly labeled
subheadings and shall not compute or narrate any ratio, difference, or combined figure that would imply a shared
basis.
6. Roles and Sign-Off
•
Analyst (case-setup or rollup engineer): Responsible for enforcing SI-internal discipline at the case level,
populating unit-bearing column headers and cell labels, and performing the Section 4 sanity check at case-output
and rollup.
•
Peer Reviewer (Technical Director or delegated PE): Responsible for confirming item 9 of the peer-review
checklist against the artifact under review; responsible for flagging any unit-bearing defect as a report defect
rather than an editorial comment.
•
Principal Engineer (stamp holder): Responsible for confirming, prior to stamp, that the conversion table is
present in report Section 1 when applicable, and that no bare-number defects remain in the deliverable.
•
Technical Director: Owner of this SOP; responsible for periodic revision, incorporation of lessons learned from
peer-review findings, and dissemination to contracted CFD hours executed on the firm's behalf.
Deviations from this SOP require written approval from the Technical Director in advance of the deviation, recorded in
the project folder.

exit_code=0
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent check of the Ocotillo resolution note and its requirements table.

Recomputes D*, D*/dx and the site/case ambient sensitivities from first principles,
tests the hard limits for every ambient basis and every candidate cell size, reads the
submitted DOCX back as the recipient would, and checks the requirements register.
"""
import csv, math, re, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
from docx import Document

NOTE = Path('/filesystem/CFDME-2025-041_resolution_note_revA.docx')
REQ = Path('/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv')
CORPUS = Path('/tmp/ahpele/corpus')

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- inputs
Q = 30.1e6                 # W, report rev B §3.3 / scoping memo §5.1
CP = 1005.0                # J/(kg K), report Appendix C
G = 9.81                   # m/s2
R_AIR = 287.05             # J/(kg K)
DX_BG = 0.5                # m, report "background" cell
DX_PLUME = 0.25            # m, level 4 plume box
DX_FIRE = 0.125            # m, level 5 fire-source zone / 0.75 D* probe

def dstar(rho, T, q=Q, cp=CP):
    return (q / (rho * cp * T * math.sqrt(G))) ** 0.4

def isa_p(z_m):
    return 101325.0 * (1.0 - 2.25577e-5 * z_m) ** 5.25588

def band_util(R):
    """Two-sided band 5-10: return (passes, utilisation, side)."""
    if R < 5:
        return False, 5.0 / R, 'below 5'
    if R > 10:
        return False, R / 10.0, 'above 10'
    return True, max(R / 10.0, 5.0 / R), 'inside'

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- calculations
D_report = dstar(1.204, 293.15)
D_site_35 = dstar(isa_p(750)/(R_AIR*308.15), 308.15)
D_site_42 = dstar(isa_p(750)/(R_AIR*315.15), 315.15)
D_case_pT = dstar(26500/(R_AIR*223.0), 223.0)
D_case_rho = dstar(0.4, 223.0)
D_case_log = dstar(26500/(R_AIR*308.15), 308.15)
D_fixed_rho_42 = dstar(1.204, 315.15)

cases = []
for label, D in [
    ('report/scoping (rho=1.204, T=293.15 K)', D_report),
    ('site 750 m, 35 C', D_site_35),
    ('site 750 m, 42 C', D_site_42),
    ('case archive p=26.5 kPa, T=223 K', D_case_pT),
    ('case archive rho=0.4 kg/m3, T=223 K', D_case_rho),
    ('case log p=26.5 kPa, T=308.15 K', D_case_log),
    ('rho fixed 1.204, T=315.15 K (not physical)', D_fixed_rho_42),
]:
    for dx in (0.125, 0.25, 0.5):
        R = D / dx
        ok, util, side = band_util(R)
        cases.append((label, D, dx, R, ok, util, side))

print('D* recomputed (Q=30.1 MW):')
print(f'  report basis              D* = {D_report:.3f} m')
print(f'  site 750 m, 35 C          D* = {D_site_35:.3f} m')
print(f'  site 750 m, 42 C          D* = {D_site_42:.3f} m')
print(f'  case p=26.5 kPa, T=223 K  D* = {D_case_pT:.3f} m')
print(f'  case rho=0.4, T=223 K     D* = {D_case_rho:.3f} m')
print(f'  case log p=26.5, T=308.15 D* = {D_case_log:.3f} m')
print()
print('D*/dx for every ambient basis and candidate cell size (band 5-10):')
print(f'{"basis":44s} {"D* (m)":>7s} {"dx (m)":>7s} {"R":>7s} {"pass":>5s} {"util":>6s} {"side":>8s}')
for label,D,dx,R,ok,util,side in cases:
    print(f'{label:44s} {D:7.3f} {dx:7.3f} {R:7.2f} {str(ok):>5s} {util:6.2f} {side:>8s}')

# Worst case per limit
worst_band = max(cases, key=lambda c: c[5])
print(f'\nWorst D*/dx band case: {worst_band[0]}, dx={worst_band[2]} m, R={worst_band[3]:.2f}, utilisation={worst_band[5]:.2f} ({worst_band[6]}).')
worst_fire = max((c for c in cases if c[2] == DX_FIRE), key=lambda c: c[5])
print(f'Worst fire-region case: {worst_fire[0]}, R={worst_fire[3]:.2f}, utilisation={worst_fire[5]:.2f}.')
reported_R = 3.76 / DX_BG
print(f'Reported 7.5 check: 3.76 m / 0.5 m = {reported_R:.2f} (report says 7.52/7.5).')
print(f'Fire-region check: 3.74 m / 0.125 m = {D_report/DX_FIRE:.2f}; with 3.76 m = {3.76/DX_FIRE:.2f}.')
print(f'Plume-box check: 3.74 m / 0.25 m = {D_report/DX_PLUME:.2f}.')
print(f'Site check: 3.88 m / 0.125 m = {D_site_35/DX_FIRE:.2f}.')
print(f'Case-archive check: 6.40 m / 0.125 m = {D_case_pT/DX_FIRE:.2f}; 6.49 m / 0.125 m = {D_case_rho/DX_FIRE:.2f}.')
print(f'Band-allowable dx for D*=3.74 m: {D_report/10:.3f} m to {D_report/5:.3f} m.')

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- requirements table
required_cols = ['req_id','item','statement','document','revision_status','clause','value','unit','applies_to','source_candidates','verification']
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(REQ, encoding='utf-8')))
assert rows, 'requirements.csv is empty'
assert list(rows[0].keys()) == required_cols, f'bad columns: {list(rows[0].keys())}'
ids = set()
for i, r in enumerate(rows, 2):
    assert r['req_id'] and r['req_id'] not in ids, f'row {i}: duplicate/blank req_id'
    ids.add(r['req_id'])
    for c in required_cols:
        if c in ('value','unit'):
            continue
        assert r[c].strip(), f'row {i} ({r["req_id"]}): blank {c}'
    assert re.search(r'R\d{4}', r['source_candidates']), f'row {i}: no candidate ID'
    # value and unit must be both present or both absent; a numeric value must carry a unit
    assert bool(r['value'].strip()) == bool(r['unit'].strip()), f'row {i}: value/unit mismatch'
    if re.search(r'\d', r['value']):
        assert r['unit'].strip(), f'row {i}: numeric value without unit'
print(f'\nrequirements.csv: {len(rows)} rows, {len(ids)} unique IDs, all required columns populated.')

# hard-limit rows the note depends on
by_id = {r['req_id']: r for r in rows}
assert by_id['Q-01']['value'] == '5 to 10'
assert by_id['Q-03']['value'] == '0.8'
assert by_id['Q-04']['value'] == '10'
assert by_id['Q-01']['unit'] == 'dimensionless'
assert '29.9' in by_id['Q-01']['verification']
assert 'NOT MET' in by_id['Q-01']['verification'].upper()

# register check against the cited source documents
res = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '/tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_reqscan.py', '--register', str(REQ)],
                     capture_output=True, text=True)
print(res.stdout.strip())
assert res.returncode == 0, 'requirements register check failed'
assert 'notfound=0' in res.stdout and 'multi=0' in res.stdout

# peer-candidate coverage
res2 = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '/tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_reqscan.py', '--check'],
                      capture_output=True, text=True)
assert res2.returncode == 0, 'requirement candidate coverage check failed'
assert '0 not reviewed yet' in res2.stdout, res2.stdout
print(res2.stdout.splitlines()[0])


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- record cross-checks
print('\nRecord cross-checks against the source documents:')
def read_corpus(rel):
    return (CORPUS / rel).read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')

qa = read_corpus('Firm/QA/CFDME_QA_Verification_Standard_rev3.pdf.txt')
model = read_corpus('Firm/Standards/CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf.txt')
report = read_corpus('Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Reports/CFDME-2025-041_Phase1_report_revB.docx.txt')
scoping = read_corpus('Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Reports/CFDME-2025-041_scoping_memo_20251008.docx.txt')
meshlog = read_corpus('Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Case/logs/log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt.txt')
solvelog = read_corpus('Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Case/logs/log.solve_20251009_attempt3.txt.txt')
study = read_corpus('Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Case/verification/three_grid_study_outputs.txt.txt')
case_setup = read_corpus('Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Case/system_archive/OAS_case_setup_from_DWA.txt.txt')

checks_records = [
    ('QA VS rev 3 current', 'Revision: rev 3' in qa and 'Effective Date: 07/01/2025' in qa and 'Supersedes: rev 2' in qa),
    ('Modeling rev 4 current', 'rev 4' in model and 'Effective 08/15/2025' in model and 'Supersedes: rev 3' in model),
    ('Report states Q=30.1 MW', '30.1 MW' in report),
    ('Report states D*=3.76 m', '3.76 m' in report),
    ('Report states dx=0.5 m background', 'background dx = 0.5 m' in report and 'Fine-grid background cell size, dx | 0.5 m' in report),
    ('Report states reported R=7.5', 'Plume resolution index, D*/dx | 7.5' in report),
    ('Report states Pope 84%', '84 %' in report or '84%' in report),
    ('Report says two extra fire refinement levels', 'two additional refinement levels' in report),
    ('Report says fine grid retained', 'fine grid (background dx = 0.5 m) is retained' in report),
    ('Scoping memo states D*=3.76 m', 'D* = 3.76 m' in scoping),
    ('Scoping memo states dx=0.5 m / R=7.5', 'dx = 0.5 m' in scoping and 'D* / dx = 3.76 / 0.5 = 7.5' in scoping),
    ('Mesh log plume box level 4', 'Refinement level 4 for all cells inside refinementBox_plume' in meshlog),
    ('Mesh log plumeSource level 5 within 3 m', 'OAS-WUI-01_revC_plumeSource.eMesh  : level 5 within 3.00 m' in meshlog),
    ('Three-grid study reports 3.76 / 7.52 / 0.84', 'D* = 3.76 m' in study and '7.52' in study and '0.84' in study),
    ('Solve log is steady SIMPLE/k-epsilon', 'steady solve' in solvelog and 'SIMPLE' in solvelog and 'kEpsilon' in solvelog),
    ('Case setup is DWA-derived / 26.5 kPa / 223 K / 0.4', 'Built from : CFDME-2024-018' in case_setup and '26,500 Pa' in case_setup and '223 K' in case_setup and '0.4 kg/m3' in case_setup),
    ('Live controlDict lacks maxCo/maxDeltaT/adjustable', 'adjustTimeStep  no' in (Path('/filesystem/Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Case/system/controlDict').read_text()) and 'maxCo' not in Path('/filesystem/Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Case/system/controlDict').read_text() and 'maxDeltaT' not in Path('/filesystem/Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Case/system/controlDict').read_text()),
]
for name, ok in checks_records:
    print(f'  {"PASS" if ok else "FAIL"} {name}')
    assert ok, name

# hard numeric requirements mapped to computed / record values
limit_results = {
    'Q-01': (f'R at dx=0.125 m = {D_report/DX_FIRE:.2f}; band 5-10', 5 <= D_report/DX_FIRE <= 10),
    'Q-03': ('reported 0.84 >= 0.80 (but traceability not established)', 0.84 >= 0.8),
    'Q-04': ('reported 20+ cycles >= 10 cycles (window not stated)', 20 >= 10),
    'M-07': ('live controlDict has no maxCo; three-grid summaries 0.87-0.90', False),
    'M-08': ('live controlDict has no maxDeltaT; required <0.01 s typical', False),
    'M-09': ('live controlDict writeControl timeStep, writeInterval 100 steps; no 25 samples/period', False),
    'M-10': ('report asserts 20+ cycles; no transient LES log/window', False),
    'M-11': ('reported 0.87 Hz, period 1.15 s', True),
    'S-01': ('no production LES case logs on file', False),
    'S-02': ('no production 20-cycle histories on file', False),
    'S-06': ('delivery 11/07/2025', True),
    'P-01': ('checklist item 4 OPEN', False),
    'B-01': ('reported 7.5 on 0.5 m background; actual 29.9 on 0.125 m', False),
    'U-02': ('D* ambient does not match case setup/log', False),
}
print('\nHard numeric requirements checked against computed/record values:')
for rid, (desc, ok) in limit_results.items():
    assert rid in by_id, f'missing requirement {rid}'
    print(f'  {rid:5s} {"PASS" if ok else "FAIL/OPEN":9s} {desc}')

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- read the note back
assert NOTE.exists(), f'missing {NOTE}'
doc = Document(NOTE)
paras = [p.text for p in doc.paragraphs]
table_text = []
for t in doc.tables:
    for row in t.rows:
        table_text.append(' | '.join(c.text for c in row.cells))
text = '\n'.join(paras + table_text)
assert len(doc.tables) >= 3, 'expected the metadata and result tables'
for t in doc.tables:
    for row in t.rows:
        for cell in row.cells:
            assert cell.text.strip() or True  # empty spacers allowed in metadata
# key values and units must be in the read-back text
checks = {
    'D* 3.74 m': '3.74 m',
    'dx 0.125 m': '0.125 m',
    'R 29.9': '29.9',
    'R 30.1': '30.1',
    'band 5 to 10': '5 to 10',
    'site D* 3.88 m': '3.88 m',
    'site R 31.0': '31.0',
    'case D* 6.40': '6.40',
    'case R 51.2': '51.2',
    'Pope 84%': '84%',
    'DWA p=26,500 Pa': '26,500 Pa',
    'can close': 'cannot close',
    'settle': 'What would settle it',
    'probe inside': 'Nominally, yes',
    'decision': 'needs your decision',
}
for name, needle in checks.items():
    assert needle in text, f'note missing {name!r} ({needle!r})'

# no contradictory claim that the 5-10 band is met at the fire cell
assert 'band is not met' in text.lower() or 'not met' in text.lower()
assert 'D*/dx = 29.9' in text
assert '0.125 m' in text
assert '7.52' in text

# headings and signature
for h in ['Answer in brief','Basis reviewed','Where the plume resolution index lands',
          'What the resolution acceptance rests on','Was the resolved-energy figure taken inside',
          'Do the ambient values behind D* represent the site','Conformance and disposition',
          'Scope and limitations']:
    assert any(h in p for p in paras), f'missing heading {h!r}'
assert 'Gordon Selby, PE' in text and 'Marguerite Falk, PE' in text
print(f'\nDOCX: {len(doc.paragraphs)} paragraphs, {len(doc.tables)} tables, {len(text.split())} words — all key values present.')
