Tucson, Arizona  |  CFDME-2025-041  |  rev A
MEMORANDUM — LES RESOLUTION BASIS (PEER-REVIEW CHECKLIST ITEM 4)
Ocotillo Additive Structures — WUI Wildfire, Phase 1
1.  The fine grid the report uses is at D*/dx = 29.9 (dimensionless), or 30.1 using the report’s rounded D* = 3.76 m — not 7.5.  The plume length scale recomputes to D* = 3.74 m for Q = 30.1 MW on the report’s ambient basis, but the representative fire-region cell is dx = 0.125 m, not the 0.5 m background cell.  The firm’s band of 5 to 10 is not met: the fire region is about three times over-resolved, not under-resolved.
2.  Resolution acceptance currently rests on the scoping-memo value 7.5, computed on the 0.5 m background cell, and on a three-grid table.  Under QA Verification Standard rev 3 neither is valid LES verification.  The only alternative acceptance route on file is the 84% Pope figure, and that figure is not traceable to an LES solve, probe record or averaging data.
3.  Checklist item 4 cannot close on the present record.  It can close without a new run only if (a) the Verification section is revised to report the actual dx and D*/dx, with a substantiated Pope fraction and its probe/averaging window, and (b) you decide that the resulting over-resolution (D*/dx above 10) is acceptable and documented and that the Pope criterion alone carries acceptance.  If the existing LES output cannot support the 84%, or you do not accept D*/dx above 10, the item stays open and needs a new LES run or a written deviation.  No new run is included here.
1.  Basis reviewed
As of 10/09/2025, from the file server only; no new run, mesh or post-processing.  Governing documents are QA Verification Standard — Mesh & Resolution rev 3 (effective 07/01/2025, supersedes rev 2), CFD Modeling Standards — Fire & Buoyant Flows rev 4 (effective 08/15/2025, supersedes rev 3), SOW CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01 (signed 10/08/2025), and the Phase 1 scoping memo rev A (10/08/2025, prepared by Gordon Selby and concurred by Marguerite Falk).  The item under review is Phase 1 draft report rev B (10/09/2025, draft, unreviewed, unsealed) and peer-review checklist item 4 (opened 10/09/2025, OPEN).  The run record consists of the mesh log log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt, solver log log.solve_20251009_attempt3.txt, and the three-grid study outputs (all 10/09/2025); the site record is site_met_avra_valley_2015-2024.csv and the structural wind-load basis memo rev A (10/09/2025, for the ~750 m site elevation).  Superseded QA rev 2 and Modeling rev 3 are not applied.
2.  Where the plume resolution index lands
The fire is Q = 30.1 MW = 30.1 × 10^6 W over the 3.0 m front segment (report §3.3; scoping memo §5.1).  QA Verification Standard rev 3 §2 defines D* = [Q / (rho_inf · cp · T_inf · sqrt(g))]^(2/5).  With the report’s ambient values — rho_inf = 1.204 kg/m³, cp = 1005 J/(kg·K), T_inf = 293.15 K, g = 9.81 m/s² — the recomputed value is D* = 3.74 m.  The report and scoping memo state 3.76 m; the 0.5% difference is arithmetic/rounding and does not change the conclusion.
The cell size is the point at issue.  Report Appendix C labels dx = 0.5 m as the “fine-grid background cell size”, and scoping memo §5.1 uses the same value.  But report §6.2 says the fire-source refinement zone carries two additional refinement levels above background on every grid, and the mesh log confirms it: the log sets level 4 inside refinementBox_plume (0.25 m) and level 5 within 3.00 m of the plumeSource surface (0.125 m) relative to the 0.5 m level-3 background.  Two levels above the 0.5 m background is 0.125 m.  The 0.75·D* probe used for the Pope figure is 2.81 m above the source top for D* = 3.74 m, inside that 3.00 m level-5 zone.
Taking dx = 0.125 m as the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region — the definition in QA Verification Standard rev 3 §2 and §5.1 — gives:
D*/dx = 3.74 m / 0.125 m = 29.9  (dimensionless);  with the report’s 3.76 m, 30.1.
The reported 7.5 is arithmetically correct only for the 0.5 m background cell: 3.76 m / 0.5 m = 7.52.  It is not the index of the fire region.  Table 1 shows the alternatives.
Table 1 — Plume resolution index on candidate cell sizes and ambient bases.  D* recomputed from Q = 30.1 MW; the last two rows are explained in Section 5.  The mesh log's final summary labels L3 (0.5 m) “plume core”, but its refinement settings put the plume box at L4 (0.25 m) and plumeSource at L5 (0.125 m), matching report §6.2's two-level fire-source refinement; the stricter fire-source reading is used above.
The band is two-sided: QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5.1 requires 5 to 10.  At 29.9 the upper bound is exceeded by a factor of 2.99 (utilisation 2.99); the lower bound is not at issue.  For D* = 3.74 m the band would require dx between 0.374 m and 0.748 m; the actual 0.125 m cell is 3.0 times finer than the lower end of that range.  The correct characterisation is over-resolution: the mesh is finer than the band’s upper bound, not coarser than its lower bound.  That is a compute-cost and conformity issue, not a physical under-resolution of the plume.  Applying the same two-level correction to the three-grid study gives D*/dx = 15.0 (coarse), 21.5 (medium) and 30.1 (fine) instead of the reported 3.76, 5.37 and 7.52 — no grid in the study is in the band.
3.  What the resolution acceptance rests on
QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5 accepts either of two LES criteria: D*/dx in the band 5 to 10 (§5.1), or Pope k_res/(k_res + k_sgs) ≥ 0.8 (§5.2).  Either alone is acceptable; both are preferred and are the default expectation for authorities-having-jurisdiction or life-safety end use.  Section 6 requires Q, D*, dx, D*/dx and the Pope fraction — with probe location and averaging window — in the Verification body, not an appendix, and states that GCI values shall not appear in LES deliverables.  A three-grid table may be retained only in an appendix labelled as a sensitivity study; it is not verification evidence for LES.
The project record rests on two things that do not meet that standard.  First, the 7.5 in the scoping memo and report is computed on the 0.5 m background cell, not the 0.125 m fire-region cell.  Marguerite Falk reviewed and concurred with the scoping memo on 10/08/2025, so it is a signed project basis, but it is not the dx that QA Verification Standard rev 3 §2 defines for the buoyancy-dominated region.  Second, report §6.1 presents a three-grid comparison of T_peak and U_z,peak as the verification evidence.  The values are non-monotonic (T_peak 1420 / 1487 / 1461 K; U_z,peak 12.8 / 11.2 / 12.4 m/s).  Under QA rev 3 §4 and §6, non-monotonicity is an expected consequence of the changing resolved/modelled split in LES, not a discretisation-error tail; no GCI can be formed, and a three-grid table in the body of an LES report is non-compliant whether or not a GCI band accompanies it.  The table may be moved to an appendix as a sensitivity study only.
That leaves the Pope route as the only possible acceptance basis on file.  The 84% figure appears in the fine-grid summary of three_grid_study_outputs.txt and in report Appendix C.  It is attached to the fluid-only three-grid study (11,196,000 cells), not the production mesh (11,214,862 cells), and it is not stated in §6.1; the record gives no k_res/k_sgs values, no probe coordinates and no averaging start/end or sample count.  The only solver log on file, log.solve_20251009_attempt3.txt, is a steady SIMPLE/k-epsilon attempt (800 outer iterations, residual plateau, not converged) on the production mesh — not a transient LES.  The live Case/system/controlDict is also not the transient control required by Modeling Standard rev 4 §4: it has adjustTimeStep no, no maxCo, no maxDeltaT, and writeControl timeStep.  On the present file server the 84% cannot be independently verified and the resolution claim cannot be traced to an LES result.  If attempt 3 is the run of record, QA §4 applies instead and requires a RANS GCI with observed p, refinement ratios and Fs = 1.25; that evidence is also absent.
This is the point that needs your decision, because QA Verification Standard rev 3 is your document as author of record and you are the Reviewing Engineer: (i) whether D*/dx above 10 on the 0.125 m fire-region cell is a documented over-resolution to be accepted, or a nonconformance requiring revision — this also confirms the dx reading, because if §5.1 were read as permitting the 0.5 m background the index would be 7.5 and the band would appear to be met; and (ii) whether the existing 84% record is sufficient to carry acceptance on the Pope criterion alone, or must be reproduced from traceable LES output.  The standard calls values above 10 “wasteful of compute”, not inadequate, so the over-resolution reading is available; it is not available for an unsubstantiated Pope figure.
4.  Was the resolved-energy figure taken inside the region the index describes?
Nominally, yes.  The 84% is stated at the plume-centreline probe located 0.75·D* above the source top surface (report Appendix C; three_grid_study_outputs.txt).  With D* = 3.74 m that is 2.81 m above the source top, on the plume axis, inside the 3.00 m level-5 refined zone and inside the buoyancy-dominated flow.  It is a point on the plume axis, not a domain average; a domain average would be dominated by quiescent ambient cells and would not represent the plume.
The location is therefore acceptable in principle; the evidentiary support is not.  The figure is a single point with no k_res/k_sgs values, no averaging start/end or sample count, and no probe record in the solve log.  The solve log’s probes are at z = 4 m, 8 m and 12 m AGL, not at the 0.75·D* ≈ 2.8 m elevation; no probe file or monitor history for the 84% is on the server.  The answer is therefore: yes on intended location, but not demonstrated by the record.  If the 84% were a volume or domain average it would not satisfy QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5.2; the record does not let that be checked either way.
5.  Do the ambient values behind D* represent the site?
No.  The D* behind the reported 7.5 uses rho_inf = 1.204 kg/m³ and T_inf = 293.15 K (20 °C), i.e. sea-level 20 °C air.  The site design envelope is 35–42 °C, 10–25% RH and 5–12 m/s at 20 ft (scoping memo §2; SOW §3.1), at a ground elevation of about 750 m (structural wind-load basis memo §2.1a).  At 750 m the ISA pressure is 92.6 kPa, not 101.3 kPa.
The site effect is modest if density is computed consistently.  At fixed pressure D* depends on rho·T = p/R, so the site temperature cancels; the elevation lowers the pressure and raises D*.  At 35–42 °C and 92.6 kPa, rho = 1.047–1.024 kg/m³ and D* = 3.88 m, 3.7% above the report basis.  At dx = 0.125 m that gives D*/dx = 31.0, still above 10; at dx = 0.5 m it gives 7.76, inside the band only because the background cell is being used.  Holding rho = 1.204 kg/m³ and simply heating the air to 42 °C is not a thermodynamically consistent state; it would give D* = 3.64 m and D*/dx = 29.1, still outside the band.  Site conditions therefore do not bring the fire-region index into 5–10.
A more serious ambient problem is in the case record.  The only case-setup archive on file, OAS_case_setup_from_DWA.txt §3, records p_inf = 26,500 Pa, T_inf = 223 K and rho_inf = 0.4 kg/m³, inherited verbatim from the Dry Wash Aerospace high-altitude case.  At that pressure D* = 6.40 m (6.49 m using the stated 0.4 kg/m³), giving D*/dx = 51.2 at 0.125 m (51.9 using 6.49 m) and 12.8 even at the report’s 0.5 m background — outside the band on either cell.  The solve log initialises T at 308.15 K (35 °C), so the archive and the log do not agree; the actual p/T/rho used by the LES is not documented.  The Dry Wash validation memo §5 expressly limits that case to high-altitude, low-density, non-reacting aerodynamics and says it is not validated for ground-level reacting buoyant flow; Modeling Standard rev 4 §7 prohibits pulling it forward without a full physics rebuild.
Conclusion: the ambient behind the reported D* is not site-representative, and the case record is internally inconsistent.  Correcting D* to the site gives 3.88 m and does not fix the band; using the case-archive ambient would make the index about 51.  Before any resolution figure is relied on, the actual p/T/rho used by the LES must be documented and D* recomputed.  That work belongs with the project engineer; it also bears on checklist items 2 and 3, which this note does not decide.
6.  Conformance and disposition of checklist item 4
Table 2 — Conformance of the present record with QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5–§7.
Disposition: checklist item 4 cannot close on the present record.  The decisive reason is not that the fire mesh is too coarse — it is finer than the band’s upper bound — but that the 7.5 is measured on the background cell while the fire-region cell is 0.125 m, so the actual D*/dx is 29.9–30.1 and §5.1 is not met; and the only alternative acceptance route, the 84% Pope figure, is not supported by a traceable LES calculation in the Verification body.  The report also places the values in Appendix C and presents a three-grid table as verification, both contrary to §6.
Project engineer (G. Selby / R. Ellsworth) to issue a Verification addendum to report rev B (rev C) before the 11/07/2025 review.  It should report Q = 30.1 MW, D* = 3.74 m recomputed (or the documented case value), dx = 0.125 m, D*/dx = 29.9 (30.1 with 3.76 m) and state plainly that the 5–10 band is exceeded on the high side and the mesh is over-resolved.  Cite the snappy log level-5 setting and the 3.00 m plume-source zone.
Provide a traceable Pope calculation from the existing LES output: k_res and k_sgs at the stated probe coordinates, the averaging start and end times, the number of puffing cycles and the sample count.  The window must be at least 10 cycles (≈11.5 s at the 1.15 s period).  If the existing fields or monitor history do not contain these quantities, say so; the 84% then cannot be produced without a new LES run.
Document the ambient basis actually used by the LES (p, T, rho) and recompute D* from it.  Reconcile the DWA-derived case archive with the log initialisation (T = 308.15 K).  Show the site value (D* = 3.88 m at 750 m and 35–42 °C) alongside it.
Move the three-grid table to an appendix labelled as a sensitivity study; remove it from §6 and do not present it as verification or compute a GCI from it.  Move all five resolution values into §6 with the probe location and averaging window.
Reviewing Engineer (M. Falk) to record the decision in two parts: (i) whether D*/dx = 29.9 is accepted as documented over-resolution under QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5.1, or treated as a nonconformance requiring revision; and (ii) whether the Pope 84% is accepted as the sole acceptance criterion under §5.2.  If either answer is no, item 4 remains open and requires either a new LES run or a written deviation approved by the Reviewing Engineer and the Owner.
If the existing LES output supports the 84% with a stated window and the report is revised as above, item 4 can close on the Pope criterion even though D*/dx is above 10, because QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5 accepts either criterion alone.  If the existing output does not support it, or if you require strict compliance with the 5–10 band, the item cannot close without a new LES run.  No new run is included in this note; the production LES runs in report Appendix B are scheduled separately for Sprint 2 (10/20/2025) and are not on file.
What can be reused: the fine mesh is geometrically well formed (checkMesh “Mesh OK”, maximum non-orthogonality 58.34°, maximum skewness 2.14), and the rev C geometry and refined fire-source region are usable; the boundary-condition framework can be retained, but the solver, radiation and combustion setup must be rebuilt to Modeling Standard rev 4.  What cannot be reused is the 7.5 resolution claim, the three-grid table as verification evidence, or the 84% without its supporting data.
7.  Scope and limitations
This note decides only peer-review checklist item 4 (resolution basis).  Items 2 (regime), 3 (solver package), 5 (through-wall treatment), 6 (validation), 7 (geometry revision) and 9 (wind-pressure units) remain open and are not decided or implied to be closed here.  The report under review is draft rev B and unsealed; this note does not release it or provide a Reviewing Engineer signature.  No new run, mesh refinement, post-processing or field extraction has been performed.  The only solver log available is the steady attempt 3; no wildfire LES monitor history or wildfire LES field data were found on the file server during this review.

# Independent review — CFDME-2025-041 resolution note rev A

Reviewed deliverable: `/filesystem/CFDME-2025-041_resolution_note_revA.docx` (DOCX 5 pages, 3 tables, 3,222 words; `ahpele_check.py` clean). I did not modify it.

Governing record checked: QA Verification Standard — Mesh & Resolution rev 3 (effective 07/01/2025); CFD Modeling Standards — Fire & Buoyant Flows rev 4 (effective 08/15/2025); SOW CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01 (10/08/2025); Phase 1 scoping memo rev A (10/08/2025); Phase 1 report rev B (10/09/2025); peer-review checklist item 4; mesh/solver logs; three-grid study; site met CSV; wind-load basis memo.

## Findings

1. **MAJOR — The note’s central answer (D*/dx = 29.9, “not 7.5”) rests on a cell size that the mesh log’s own final refinement distribution calls the wall boundary layer, not the plume core; the log is internally contradictory and the note does not resolve it.**
   - Requirement: QA Verification Standard rev 3 §2 and §5.1: dx is “the representative fire-region cell edge length” / “the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region”; the index must be computed on that representative cell.
   - Deliverable has: Section 2 chooses dx = 0.125 m (the level-5 `plumeSource` distance refinement within 3.00 m) as “the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region”, giving 29.9. Table 1 note acknowledges: “The mesh log’s final summary labels L3 (0.5 m) ‘plume core’, but its refinement settings put the plume box at L4 (0.25 m) and plumeSource at L5 (0.125 m) … the stricter fire-source reading is used above.”
   - What the mesh log actually says: the final refinement distribution (`log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt`, lines 970–981) labels **L3 (dx = 0.5 m) “fine grid target, plume core”**, L4 (0.25 m) “near-wall transition”, L5 (0.125 m) “wall boundary layer + slab”, L6 “wall assembly, cavity”, L7 “steel ties + tie-concrete interface”. The log header (lines 38–39) says “Fine grid dx = 0.5 m sized against D* = 3.76 m … D*/dx = 7.52 targets the 5-10 band”, and the verification cross-check (lines 1100–1105) says “Resolution basis: D*/dx = 7.52 lies inside the [5, 10] band”. The refinement settings (lines 56–93) separately say level 4 inside `refinementBox_plume` and level 5 within 3.00 m of `plumeSource`. The log therefore contradicts itself on which cell is the plume core, and it states 7.52 as the resolution basis in two other places. The note picks the L5 setting and dismisses the final “plume core” label without a cell-size audit or addressing the header/cross-check.
   - Should be: Resolve the contradiction before asserting the index. If the final distribution is the intended mesh (L3 0.5 m = plume core), the report’s 7.5 is the plume-core index and the band is met; if the L5 `plumeSource` cell is the correct fire-source cell, the index is 29.9. The note should extract the actual cell size on the plume axis at the 0.75·D* probe (or state the cell-size distribution/volume fraction) and then give the index for that cell. At present the note’s “not 7.5” and “band not met” conclusions are not established against the final mesh summary.
   - Evidence: `log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt` lines 970–981 (“L3 (dx = 0.5 m) : 128 872 cells (fine grid target, plume core)”; “L4 … near-wall transition”; “L5 … wall boundary layer + slab”) versus lines 56–93 (“Refinement level 4 … refinementBox_plume”; “level 5 within 3.00 m” of `plumeSource`); report rev B §6.2 (“fire-source refinement zone carries two additional refinement levels”); note Section 2 and Table 1 note. Computed: 3.74/0.5 = 7.48; 3.74/0.25 = 15.0; 3.74/0.125 = 29.9.

2. **MAJOR — The note accepts a 10-cycle Pope averaging window without requiring the project’s 20-cycle run/statistics span (about 23 s).**
   - Requirement: Modeling Standard rev 4 §4: “Simulated end times shall span a minimum of 20 puffing periods after the initial transient has cleared, so that averages, spectra, and RMS quantities are formed on a statistically meaningful window. For a 3.0 m fire that is a simulated interval of no less than approximately 23 seconds of physical time, exclusive of startup.” SOW §3.1: “Each case shall be run to a physical simulated time covering not fewer than twenty (20) puffing cycles of the plume as characterized in Consultant’s scoping memo.”
   - Deliverable has: Section 6.2 item 2: “The window must be at least 10 cycles (≈11.5 s at the 1.15 s period).” Table 2 row: “Pope time-average ≥10 puffing cycles (§5.2) … 1.15 s period gives ≥11.5 s window.” `asks.md` A2/A6 repeats 10 cycles.
   - Should be: The existing LES run/statistics must span at least 20 cycles (≈23 s) from the SOW/Modeling Standard; QA §5.2’s “typically ten or more” is a floor, not the project requirement. If the existing LES output only supports a 10-cycle window, it does not satisfy the project basis and cannot close item 4. The report itself (§5.3) and the three-grid study assert “20+ cycles”, so the note should require those 20+ cycles to be substantiated rather than accepting 10.
   - Evidence: Modeling Standard rev 4 §4 (p. 3); SOW §3.1 (p. 2); report rev B §5.3; three-grid study header/fine summary (“20+ puffing cycles sampled”, t = 40.0 s); note Section 6.2 item 2 and Table 2. Period check: 1/0.87 Hz = 1.15 s; 20 × 1.15 s = 23.0 s.
---MID---
6. **MAJOR — The note calls the refined fire-source region “usable” for reuse even though it is the 0.125 m region that produces D*/dx = 29.9 and fails the band (or, on the final mesh summary, it is the wall-boundary-layer region, not the plume core).**
   - Requirement: QA rev 3 §5.1 (band 5–10) and §5.2 (Pope alternative); Modeling rev 4 §7 (physics/regime rebuild on reuse, including freestream/inlet conditions).
   - Deliverable has: Section 6.4: “the fine mesh is geometrically well formed … and the rev C geometry and refined fire-source region are usable; the boundary-condition framework can be retained, but the solver, radiation and combustion setup must be rebuilt”.
   - Should be: The refined fire-source region is geometrically well formed but is over-resolved for §5.1; reusing it on a new LES run will still give D*/dx ≈ 30 (or the region is a wall-boundary refinement) unless the Pope route is substantiated or a deviation is accepted, or the fire region is coarsened to dx ≈ 0.374–0.748 m. The reuse statement should say this explicitly. Also, Modeling §7 requires the freestream/inlet conditions (wind, temperature, humidity, density) to be rebuilt from first principles, not merely the solver/radiation/combustion; the note’s “boundary-condition framework can be retained” is acceptable only for patch topology, not the DWA ambient values.
   - Evidence: note Section 6.4; note Section 2 (dx = 0.125 m, R = 29.9); mesh log final summary (L5 = wall boundary layer + slab) and refinement settings; Modeling rev 4 §7 (p. 4); D* = 3.74 m gives allowable dx = 0.374–0.748 m for the 5–10 band.

7. **MINOR — Two citations in Table 2 are wrong.**
   - Requirement/deliverable: Table 2 row “No GCI / three-grid table as LES verification; appendix sensitivity only (§6)” says “Three-grid table in §6.1 and Appendix C”. The report’s three-grid table is Table 4 in §6.1 only; Appendix C contains the separate resolution-values table (Q, D*, dx, D*/dx, Pope), not the three-grid table. The same table row says “Appendix C asserts PASS”; report Appendix C does not assert PASS — the three-grid study output does (“LES resolution acceptance: PASS on both criteria”).
   - Should be: Cite “three-grid table in §6.1; resolution values in Appendix C” and attribute the PASS assertion to the three-grid study, not Appendix C.
   - Evidence: report rev B §6.1 Table 4 and Appendix C Table 6; three_grid_study_outputs.txt resolution assessment; note Table 2.

8. **MINOR — The note’s “3.7% above the report basis” is ambiguous and the 3.76 m scoping value is an arithmetic error, not just rounding.**
   - Requirement: note must carry accurate comparison to the report/scoping basis.
   - Deliverable has: Section 5: “D* = 3.88 m, 3.7% above the report basis”; Section 2: “The report and scoping memo state 3.76 m; the 0.5% difference is arithmetic/rounding”.
   - Should be: 3.88/3.74 = +3.7%, but 3.88/3.76 = +3.2%; state which basis. The scoping memo’s own expression (27.08)^(2/5) evaluates to 3.74 m, not 3.76 m; the 0.5% is a calculation error in the signed memo, not rounding. The note’s recomputed 3.74 m is correct.
   - Evidence: Q = 30.1 MW, rho = 1.204 kg/m³, cp = 1005 J/(kg·K), T = 293.15 K, g = 9.81 m/s² → D* = 3.742 m; scoping memo §5.1; note Sections 2 and 5.

9. **MINOR — The note says rev C geometry is “usable” while rev D was transmitted on 10/09/2025 and checklist item 7 is open.**
   - Requirement: checklist item 7 (geometry revision tagged and matches case log); note Section 7 says item 7 remains open.
   - Deliverable has: Section 6.4: “the rev C geometry and refined fire-source region are usable”.
   - Should be: Limit the statement to the mesh/case built on rev C; do not imply rev C is the final geometry while rev D (parapet, total height 3355 mm) is on the server and item 7 is undecided.
---END---
- The note correctly identifies the report’s three-grid table as non-compliant LES verification under QA rev 3 §4/§6, and correctly states GCI is not valid for LES.
- The note correctly identifies that the 84% Pope figure is on the fluid-only three-grid study (11,196,000 cells), not the production mesh (11,214,862 cells), and that the only solver log on file is the steady SIMPLE/k-epsilon attempt 3 (800 iterations, residual plateau).
- The note correctly identifies the ambient mismatch: report D* uses sea-level 20 °C air (rho = 1.204 kg/m³, T = 293.15 K); site envelope is 35–42 °C at ~750 m (ISA pressure 92.6 kPa), giving D* = 3.88 m and D*/dx = 31.0 at 0.125 m; the DWA archive ambient (26,500 Pa, 223 K, 0.4 kg/m³) gives D* = 6.40–6.49 m and D*/dx = 51.2–51.9 at 0.125 m.
- The note correctly says the item cannot close on the present record; the report’s resolution values are in Appendix C, not the Verification body, and the 84% is not supported by a traceable LES calculation on file.

## Bottom line

The note’s arithmetic is correct and its disposition (item 4 cannot close on the present record) is defensible. The decisive defect is that its headline 29.9 depends on an unresolved contradiction in the mesh log: the final refinement distribution calls L3 (0.5 m) the “plume core” and L5 (0.125 m) “wall boundary layer + slab”, while the refinement settings place the plume box at L4 and the `plumeSource` refinement at L5. If the final distribution is the intended plume-core basis, the report’s 7.5 is correct and the band is met; the note’s “not 7.5 / band not met” conclusion would be wrong. The note must audit the actual cell size on the plume axis at the 0.75·D* probe before asserting 29.9. Independently, the closure path is defective: it sets a 10-cycle averaging window where the project requires 20, treats the D*/dx over-resolution as a second gate even though QA §5 allows the Pope criterion alone, and omits the QA §3 requirement that the Verification section appear ahead of Results and state the LES SGS closure.

# Independent review — CFDME-2025-041 resolution note rev A

Reviewed deliverable: `/filesystem/CFDME-2025-041_resolution_note_revA.docx` (DOCX 5 pages, 3 tables, 3,222 words; `ahpele_check.py` clean). I did not modify it.

Governing record checked: QA Verification Standard — Mesh & Resolution rev 3 (effective 07/01/2025); CFD Modeling Standards — Fire & Buoyant Flows rev 4 (effective 08/15/2025); SOW CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01 (10/08/2025); Phase 1 scoping memo rev A (10/08/2025); Phase 1 report rev B (10/09/2025); peer-review checklist item 4; mesh/solver logs; three-grid study; site met CSV; wind-load basis memo.

## Findings

1. **MAJOR — The note’s central answer (D*/dx = 29.9, “not 7.5”) rests on a cell size that the mesh log’s own final refinement distribution calls the wall boundary layer, not the plume core; the log is internally contradictory and the note does not resolve it.**
   - Requirement: QA Verification Standard rev 3 §2 and §5.1: dx is “the representative fire-region cell edge length” / “the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region”; the index must be computed on that representative cell.
   - Deliverable has: Section 2 chooses dx = 0.125 m (the level-5 `plumeSource` distance refinement within 3.00 m) as “the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region”, giving 29.9. Table 1 note acknowledges: “The mesh log’s final summary labels L3 (0.5 m) ‘plume core’, but its refinement settings put the plume box at L4 (0.25 m) and plumeSource at L5 (0.125 m) … the stricter fire-source reading is used above.”
   - What the mesh log actually says: the final refinement distribution (`log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt`, lines 970–981) labels **L3 (dx = 0.5 m) “fine grid target, plume core”**, L4 (0.25 m) “near-wall transition”, L5 (0.125 m) “wall boundary layer + slab”, L6 “wall assembly, cavity”, L7 “steel ties + tie-concrete interface”. The log header (lines 38–39) says “Fine grid dx = 0.5 m sized against D* = 3.76 m … D*/dx = 7.52 targets the 5-10 band”, and the verification cross-check (lines 1100–1105) says “Resolution basis: D*/dx = 7.52 lies inside the [5, 10] band”. The refinement settings (lines 56–93) separately say level 4 inside `refinementBox_plume` and level 5 within 3.00 m of `plumeSource`. The log therefore contradicts itself on which cell is the plume core, and it states 7.52 as the resolution basis in two other places. The note picks the L5 setting and dismisses the final “plume core” label without a cell-size audit or addressing the header/cross-check.
   - Should be: Resolve the contradiction before asserting the index. If the final distribution is the intended mesh (L3 0.5 m = plume core), the report’s 7.5 is the plume-core index and the band is met; if the L5 `plumeSource` cell is the correct fire-source cell, the index is 29.9. The note should extract the actual cell size on the plume axis at the 0.75·D* probe (or state the cell-size distribution/volume fraction) and then give the index for that cell. At present the note’s “not 7.5” and “band not met” conclusions are not established against the final mesh summary.
   - Evidence: `log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt` lines 970–981 (“L3 (dx = 0.5 m) : 128 872 cells (fine grid target, plume core)”; “L4 … near-wall transition”; “L5 … wall boundary layer + slab”) versus lines 56–93 (“Refinement level 4 … refinementBox_plume”; “level 5 within 3.00 m” of `plumeSource`); report rev B §6.2 (“fire-source refinement zone carries two additional refinement levels”); note Section 2 and Table 1 note. Computed: 3.74/0.5 = 7.48; 3.74/0.25 = 15.0; 3.74/0.125 = 29.9.

2. **MAJOR — The note accepts a 10-cycle Pope averaging window without requiring the project’s 20-cycle run/statistics span (about 23 s).**
   - Requirement: Modeling Standard rev 4 §4: “Simulated end times shall span a minimum of 20 puffing periods after the initial transient has cleared, so that averages, spectra, and RMS quantities are formed on a statistically meaningful window. For a 3.0 m fire that is a simulated interval of no less than approximately 23 seconds of physical time, exclusive of startup.” SOW §3.1: “Each case shall be run to a physical simulated time covering not fewer than twenty (20) puffing cycles of the plume as characterized in Consultant’s scoping memo.”
   - Deliverable has: Section 6.2 item 2: “The window must be at least 10 cycles (≈11.5 s at the 1.15 s period).” Table 2 row: “Pope time-average ≥10 puffing cycles (§5.2) … 1.15 s period gives ≥11.5 s window.” `asks.md` A2/A6 repeats 10 cycles.
   - Should be: The existing LES run/statistics must span at least 20 cycles (≈23 s) from the SOW/Modeling Standard; QA §5.2’s “typically ten or more” is a floor, not the project requirement. If the existing LES output only supports a 10-cycle window, it does not satisfy the project basis and cannot close item 4. The report itself (§5.3) and the three-grid study assert “20+ cycles”, so the note should require those 20+ cycles to be substantiated rather than accepting 10.
   - Evidence: Modeling Standard rev 4 §4 (p. 3); SOW §3.1 (p. 2); report rev B §5.3; three-grid study header/fine summary (“20+ puffing cycles sampled”, t = 40.0 s); note Section 6.2 item 2 and Table 2. Period check: 1/0.87 Hz = 1.15 s; 20 × 1.15 s = 23.0 s.

3. **MAJOR — The note makes acceptance depend on both the Pope fraction and a separate “over-resolution accepted” decision, although QA rev 3 §5 expressly allows either criterion alone.**
   - Requirement: QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5: “For large-eddy simulations, the firm accepts either of the following as sufficient evidence that the resolution is adequate … Both are preferred; either alone is acceptable.” §5.2 gives the Pope route independently of §5.1.
   - Deliverable has: Answer in brief item 3: item can close only if “(a) the Verification section is revised … with a substantiated Pope fraction … and (b) you decide that the resulting over-resolution (D*/dx above 10) is acceptable and documented and that the Pope criterion alone carries acceptance.” Section 6.2 item 5: “If either answer is no, item 4 remains open and requires either a new LES run or a written deviation.”

   - Evidence: report rev B §5 “Results” (para 58) precedes §6 “Verification” (para 71); report §6 has no SGS closure statement; QA rev 3 §3/§3(a) (p. 1–2); note Section 6.2 item 4 and Table 2.

# Independent review — CFDME-2025-041 resolution note rev A

Reviewed deliverable: `/filesystem/CFDME-2025-041_resolution_note_revA.docx` (DOCX 5 pages, 3 tables, 3,222 words; `ahpele_check.py` clean). I did not modify it.

Governing record checked: QA Verification Standard — Mesh & Resolution rev 3 (effective 07/01/2025); CFD Modeling Standards — Fire & Buoyant Flows rev 4 (effective 08/15/2025); SOW CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01 (10/08/2025); Phase 1 scoping memo rev A (10/08/2025); Phase 1 report rev B (10/09/2025); peer-review checklist item 4; mesh/solver logs; three-grid study; site met CSV; wind-load basis memo.

## Findings

1. **MAJOR — The note’s central answer (D*/dx = 29.9, “not 7.5”) rests on a cell size that the mesh log’s own final refinement distribution calls the wall boundary layer, not the plume core; the log is internally contradictory and the note does not resolve it.**
   - Requirement: QA Verification Standard rev 3 §2 and §5.1: dx is “the representative fire-region cell edge length” / “the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region”; the index must be computed on that representative cell.
   - Deliverable has: Section 2 chooses dx = 0.125 m (the level-5 `plumeSource` distance refinement within 3.00 m) as “the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region”, giving 29.9. Table 1 note acknowledges: “The mesh log’s final summary labels L3 (0.5 m) ‘plume core’, but its refinement settings put the plume box at L4 (0.25 m) and plumeSource at L5 (0.125 m) … the stricter fire-source reading is used above.”
   - What the mesh log actually says: the final refinement distribution (`log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt`, lines 970–981) labels **L3 (dx = 0.5 m) “fine grid target, plume core”**, L4 (0.25 m) “near-wall transition”, L5 (0.125 m) “wall boundary layer + slab”, L6 “wall assembly, cavity”, L7 “steel ties + tie-concrete interface”. The log header (lines 38–39) says “Fine grid dx = 0.5 m sized against D* = 3.76 m … D*/dx = 7.52 targets the 5-10 band”, and the verification cross-check (lines 1100–1105) says “Resolution basis: D*/dx = 7.52 lies inside the [5, 10] band”. The refinement settings (lines 56–93) separately say level 4 inside `refinementBox_plume` and level 5 within 3.00 m of `plumeSource`. The log therefore contradicts itself on which cell is the plume core, and it states 7.52 as the resolution basis in two other places. The note picks the L5 setting and dismisses the final “plume core” label without a cell-size audit or addressing the header/cross-check.
   - Should be: Resolve the contradiction before asserting the index. If the final distribution is the intended mesh (L3 0.5 m = plume core), the report’s 7.5 is the plume-core index and the band is met; if the L5 `plumeSource` cell is the correct fire-source cell, the index is 29.9. The note should extract the actual cell size on the plume axis at the 0.75·D* probe (or state the cell-size distribution/volume fraction) and then give the index for that cell. At present the note’s “not 7.5” and “band not met” conclusions are not established against the final mesh summary.
   - Evidence: `log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt` lines 970–981 (“L3 (dx = 0.5 m) : 128 872 cells (fine grid target, plume core)”; “L4 … near-wall transition”; “L5 … wall boundary layer + slab”) versus lines 56–93 (“Refinement level 4 … refinementBox_plume”; “level 5 within 3.00 m” of `plumeSource`); report rev B §6.2 (“fire-source refinement zone carries two additional refinement levels”); note Section 2 and Table 1 note. Computed: 3.74/0.5 = 7.48; 3.74/0.25 = 15.0; 3.74/0.125 = 29.9.

2. **MAJOR — The note accepts a 10-cycle Pope averaging window without requiring the project’s 20-cycle run/statistics span (about 23 s).**
   - Requirement: Modeling Standard rev 4 §4: “Simulated end times shall span a minimum of 20 puffing periods after the initial transient has cleared, so that averages, spectra, and RMS quantities are formed on a statistically meaningful window. For a 3.0 m fire that is a simulated interval of no less than approximately 23 seconds of physical time, exclusive of startup.” SOW §3.1: “Each case shall be run to a physical simulated time covering not fewer than twenty (20) puffing cycles of the plume as characterized in Consultant’s scoping memo.”
   - Deliverable has: Section 6.2 item 2: “The window must be at least 10 cycles (≈11.5 s at the 1.15 s period).” Table 2 row: “Pope time-average ≥10 puffing cycles (§5.2) … 1.15 s period gives ≥11.5 s window.” `asks.md` A2/A6 repeats 10 cycles.
   - Should be: The existing LES run/statistics must span at least 20 cycles (≈23 s) from the SOW/Modeling Standard; QA §5.2’s “typically ten or more” is a floor, not the project requirement. If the existing LES output only supports a 10-cycle window, it does not satisfy the project basis and cannot close item 4. The report itself (§5.3) and the three-grid study assert “20+ cycles”, so the note should require those 20+ cycles to be substantiated rather than accepting 10.
   - Evidence: Modeling Standard rev 4 §4 (p. 3); SOW §3.1 (p. 2); report rev B §5.3; three-grid study header/fine summary (“20+ puffing cycles sampled”, t = 40.0 s); note Section 6.2 item 2 and Table 2. Period check: 1/0.87 Hz = 1.15 s; 20 × 1.15 s = 23.0 s.

3. **MAJOR — The note makes acceptance depend on both the Pope fraction and a separate “over-resolution accepted” decision, although QA rev 3 §5 expressly allows either criterion alone.**
   - Requirement: QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5: “For large-eddy simulations, the firm accepts either of the following as sufficient evidence that the resolution is adequate … Both are preferred; either alone is acceptable.” §5.2 gives the Pope route independently of §5.1.
   - Deliverable has: Answer in brief item 3: item can close only if “(a) the Verification section is revised … with a substantiated Pope fraction … and (b) you decide that the resulting over-resolution (D*/dx above 10) is acceptable and documented and that the Pope criterion alone carries acceptance.” Section 6.2 item 5: “If either answer is no, item 4 remains open and requires either a new LES run or a written deviation.”
   - Should be: If the Pope fraction is substantiated at ≥0.8 over the required ≥20-cycle window and stated in the Verification body, §5.2 alone is sufficient; no separate acceptance of D*/dx >10 is required, and answer (i) is not a gating condition. If the Pope route is not substantiated, then D*/dx must be in the 5–10 band (§5.1) or a deviation is required.
   - Evidence: note Answer in brief item 3 and Section 6.2 item 5; note’s own Section 3 (“Either alone is acceptable”) and Section 6.3 (“item 4 can close on the Pope criterion even though D*/dx is above 10, because QA … §5 accepts either criterion alone”); QA rev 3 §5 (p. 2).

4. **MAJOR — The note treats D*/dx above 10 as an “available” documented over-resolution under §5.1 because the standard calls it “wasteful of compute”, but §5.1 says the index “shall fall in the band 5 to 10”.**
   - Requirement: QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5.1: “The plume resolution index D*/dx … shall fall in the band 5 to 10. Values below 5 are insufficient …; values above 10 are wasteful of compute without corresponding gain in fidelity …” There is no “accept over-resolution” provision in §5.1; the only alternative acceptance route is §5.2 (Pope).
   - Deliverable has: Section 3.24: “The standard calls values above 10 ‘wasteful of compute’, not inadequate, so the over-resolution reading is available; it is not available for an unsubstantiated Pope figure.” Answer in brief item 3 and Table 2/action item 5 ask Marguerite to “accept” D*/dx = 29.9 as documented over-resolution.
   - Should be: 29.9 is a nonconformance of §5.1 on the 0.125 m cell; it can be overcome only by substantiating the §5.2 Pope criterion (either alone is acceptable) or by a written deviation. “Wasteful of compute” is explanatory, not a waiver of “shall fall in the band”.
   - Evidence: QA rev 3 §5.1 (p. 2); note Section 3.24, Answer in brief item 3, Section 6.2 item 5; computed 3.74/0.125 = 29.9 (3.76/0.125 = 30.1).

5. **MAJOR — The note’s “what would settle it” list omits two hard Verification-section requirements: the section must appear ahead of Results, and it must state the LES sub-grid closure.**
   - Requirement: QA Verification Standard rev 3 §3: the Verification section “shall … appear in the body of the report ahead of Validation and ahead of Results”; §3(a): “The turbulence treatment used (RANS, URANS, or LES) and, for LES, the sub-grid-scale closure.” §3(b): representative dx and total cell count.
   - Deliverable has: Section 6.2 item 4 only says “Move all five resolution values into §6”; Table 2 is headed “§5–§7” but includes a §3(d) row and omits §3(a), §3(b) and the §3 order requirement. The report has §5 Results before §6 Verification and does not state the LES SGS closure in §6.

# Asks in the instruction and direct answers (mirrors note sections)

## A1. Where does the plume resolution index land for the result the report rests on — with cell size and plume length scale, and is our band met?
**Answer:** The fine grid retained for the six SOW §3.1 cases (report rev B §6.3) is at **D*/dx = 29.9 (dimensionless)**, or **30.1** using the report's rounded D* = 3.76 m — not 7.5. The recomputed plume length scale is **D* = 3.74 m** for Q = 30.1 MW with the report ambient (rho = 1.204 kg/m3, cp = 1005 J/(kg K), T = 293.15 K). The representative fire-region cell is **dx = 0.125 m** (two snappy refinement levels below the 0.5 m background; level 5 within 3.00 m of the plumeSource), not the 0.5 m background cell. The firm band 5 to 10 is **NOT MET**, on the high side: the fire region is about 3x over-resolved (upper-bound utilisation 2.99). The report's 7.5 is 3.76/0.5, i.e. correct only for the background cell. Source: QA VS rev 3 §5.1; report rev B §6.2/§6.3/Appendix C; log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt; scoping memo §5.1.

## A2. What does our resolution acceptance rest on?
**Answer:** Governing basis is QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5: either D*/dx in 5–10 (§5.1) or Pope k_res/(k_res+k_sgs) >= 0.8 on a >=10-cycle time average with probes in the buoyancy-dominated flow (§5.2); either alone is acceptable, both preferred. Section 6 requires Q, D*, dx, D*/dx, Pope fraction, probe location and averaging window in the Verification body, prohibits GCI in LES deliverables, and allows a three-grid table only as an appendix sensitivity study. The project record currently rests on (a) the scoping memo 10/08/2025 value 7.5 computed on the 0.5 m background cell and (b) a three-grid table in report §6.1. Neither is valid LES verification: GCI assumes a unique grid-independent limit that LES does not have, and the table is non-monotonic (T_peak 1420/1487/1461 K; U_z 12.8/11.2/12.4 m/s). The only possible alternative is the 84% Pope figure, but it is not traceable (no k_res/k_sgs, no probe record, no averaging start/end or sample count; the only solver log on file is a steady RANS attempt, not LES). If attempt 3 is the run of record, QA VS §4 applies instead and requires a RANS GCI (observed p, refinement ratios and Fs = 1.25), which is also absent.

## A3. Does anything about that basis need a decision from Marguerite?
**Answer:** Yes, two decisions as Reviewing Engineer and author of record of QA VS rev 3:
1. Whether D*/dx = 29.9 on the 0.125 m fire-region cell (above the band's upper bound of 10) is accepted as documented over-resolution under §5.1 — QA VS calls >10 "wasteful of compute", not inadequate — or treated as a nonconformance requiring revision. This also confirms the dx reading: if §5.1 were read as allowing the 0.5 m background, the index would be 7.5 and the band would appear met.
2. Whether the existing 84% Pope record is sufficient to carry acceptance on the Pope criterion alone under §5.2, or must be reproduced from traceable LES output. If either answer is no, item 4 stays open. Marguerite also signed the 10/08/2025 scoping memo that fixed 7.5 on the 0.5 m background; the stricter QA reading (0.125 m fire-region cell) supersedes that dx value.

## A4. Was the resolved-energy figure taken inside the region the index describes?
**Answer:** Nominally yes. The 84% is at the plume-centreline probe 0.75·D* above the source top (2.81 m for D* = 3.74 m), on the plume axis inside the 3.00 m level-5 refined zone and the buoyancy-dominated flow — not a domain average. But it is a single point with no k_res/k_sgs values, no averaging start/end or sample count, and no probe record in the solve log (probes are at z = 4, 8 and 12 m AGL, not 2.8 m). So the location is acceptable in principle but the figure is not demonstrated by the record.

## A5. Do the ambient values behind D* represent the site, and what would site conditions do to it?
**Answer:** No. The reported D* uses rho = 1.204 kg/m3 and T = 293.15 K (sea-level 20 °C), while the site design envelope is 35–42 °C, 10–25% RH, 5–12 m/s at 20 ft at ~750 m elevation (wind-load basis memo §2.1a). At 750 m ISA pressure is 92.6 kPa; with consistent density, D* = 3.88 m (+3.7%) and D*/dx = 31.0 at dx = 0.125 m. Applying the same two-level correction to the three-grid study gives D*/dx = 15.0 (coarse), 21.5 (medium) and 30.1 (fine) instead of the reported 3.76, 5.37 and 7.52 — no grid in the study is in the band.
20 [Heading 1] 3.  What the resolution acceptance rests on
21 [Normal] QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5 accepts either of two LES criteria: D*/dx in the band 5 to 10 (§5.1), or Pope k_res/(k_res + k_sgs) ≥ 0.8 (§5.2).  Either alone is acceptable; both are preferred and are the default expectation for authorities-having-jurisdiction or life-safety end use.  Section 6 requires Q, D*, dx, D*/dx and the Pope fraction — with probe location and averaging window — in the Verification body, not an appendix, and states that GCI values shall not appear in LES deliverables.  A three-grid table may be retained only in an appendix labelled as a sensitivity study; it is not verification evidence for LES.
22 [Normal] The project record rests on two things that do not meet that standard.  First, the 7.5 in the scoping memo and report is computed on the 0.5 m background cell, not the 0.125 m fire-region cell.  Marguerite Falk reviewed and concurred with the scoping memo on 10/08/2025, so it is a signed project basis, but it is not the dx that QA Verification Standard rev 3 §2 defines for the buoyancy-dominated region.  Second, report §6.1 presents a three-grid comparison of T_peak and U_z,peak as the verification evidence.  The values are non-monotonic (T_peak 1420 / 1487 / 1461 K; U_z,peak 12.8 / 11.2 / 12.4 m/s).  Under QA rev 3 §4 and §6, non-monotonicity is an expected consequence of the changing resolved/modelled split in LES, not a discretisation-error tail; no GCI can be formed, and a three-grid table in the body of an LES report is non-compliant whether or not a GCI band accompanies it.  The table may be moved to an appendix as a sensitivity study only.
23 [Normal] That leaves the Pope route as the only possible acceptance basis on file.  The 84% figure appears in the fine-grid summary of three_grid_study_outputs.txt and in report Appendix C.  It is attached to the fluid-only three-grid study (11,196,000 cells), not the production mesh (11,214,862 cells), and it is not stated in §6.1; the record gives no k_res/k_sgs values, no probe coordinates and no averaging start/end or sample count.  The only solver log on file, log.solve_20251009_attempt3.txt, is a steady SIMPLE/k-epsilon attempt (800 outer iterations, residual plateau, not converged) on the production mesh — not a transient LES.  The live Case/system/controlDict is also not the transient control required by Modeling Standard rev 4 §4: it has adjustTimeStep no, no maxCo, no maxDeltaT, and writeControl timeStep.  On the present file server the 84% cannot be independently verified and the resolution claim cannot be traced to an LES result.  If attempt 3 is the run of record, QA §4 applies instead and requires a RANS GCI with observed p, refinement ratios and Fs = 1.25; that evidence is also absent.
24 [Normal] This is the point that needs your decision, because QA Verification Standard rev 3 is your document as author of record and you are the Reviewing Engineer: (i) whether D*/dx above 10 on the 0.125 m fire-region cell is a documented over-resolution to be accepted, or a nonconformance requiring revision — this also confirms the dx reading, because if §5.1 were read as permitting the 0.5 m background the index would be 7.5 and the band would appear to be met; and (ii) whether the existing 84% record is sufficient to carry acceptance on the Pope criterion alone, or must be reproduced from traceable LES output.  The standard calls values above 10 “wasteful of compute”, not inadequate, so the over-resolution reading is available; it is not available for an unsubstantiated Pope figure.
25 [Heading 1] 4.  Was the resolved-energy figure taken inside the region the index describes?
26 [Normal] Nominally, yes.  The 84% is stated at the plume-centreline probe located 0.75·D* above the source top surface (report Appendix C; three_grid_study_outputs.txt).  With D* = 3.74 m that is 2.81 m above the source top, on the plume axis, inside the 3.00 m level-5 refined zone and inside the buoyancy-dominated flow.  It is a point on the plume axis, not a domain average; a domain average would be dominated by quiescent ambient cells and would not represent the plume.
27 [Normal] The location is therefore acceptable in principle; the evidentiary support is not.  The figure is a single point with no k_res/k_sgs values, no averaging start/end or sample count, and no probe record in the solve log.  The solve log’s probes are at z = 4 m, 8 m and 12 m AGL, not at the 0.75·D* ≈ 2.8 m elevation; no probe file or monitor history for the 84% is on the server.  The answer is therefore: yes on intended location, but not demonstrated by the record.  If the 84% were a volume or domain average it would not satisfy QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5.2; the record does not let that be checked either way.
28 [Heading 1] 5.  Do the ambient values behind D* represent the site?
29 [Normal] No.  The D* behind the reported 7.5 uses rho_inf = 1.204 kg/m³ and T_inf = 293.15 K (20 °C), i.e. sea-level 20 °C air.  The site design envelope is 35–42 °C, 10–25% RH and 5–12 m/s at 20 ft (scoping memo §2; SOW §3.1), at a ground elevation of about 750 m (structural wind-load basis memo §2.1a).  At 750 m the ISA pressure is 92.6 kPa, not 101.3 kPa.
30 [Normal] The site effect is modest if density is computed consistently.  At fixed pressure D* depends on rho·T = p/R, so the site temperature cancels; the elevation lowers the pressure and raises D*.  At 35–42 °C and 92.6 kPa, rho = 1.047–1.024 kg/m³ and D* = 3.88 m, 3.7% above the report basis.  At dx = 0.125 m that gives D*/dx = 31.0, still above 10; at dx = 0.5 m it gives 7.76, inside the band only because the background cell is being used.  Holding rho = 1.204 kg/m³ and simply heating the air to 42 °C is not a thermodynamically consistent state; it would give D* = 3.64 m and D*/dx = 29.1, still outside the band.  Site conditions therefore do not bring the fire-region index into 5–10.
31 [Normal] A more serious ambient problem is in the case record.  The only case-setup archive on file, OAS_case_setup_from_DWA.txt §3, records p_inf = 26,500 Pa, T_inf = 223 K and rho_inf = 0.4 kg/m³, inherited verbatim from the Dry Wash Aerospace high-altitude case.  At that pressure D* = 6.40 m (6.49 m using the stated 0.4 kg/m³), giving D*/dx = 51.2 at 0.125 m (51.9 using 6.49 m) and 12.8 even at the report’s 0.5 m background — outside the band on either cell.  The solve log initialises T at 308.15 K (35 °C), so the archive and the log do not agree; the actual p/T/rho used by the LES is not documented.  The Dry Wash validation memo §5 expressly limits that case to high-altitude, low-density, non-reacting aerodynamics and says it is not validated for ground-level reacting buoyant flow; Modeling Standard rev 4 §7 prohibits pulling it forward without a full physics rebuild.
32 [Normal] Conclusion: the ambient behind the reported D* is not site-representative, and the case record is internally inconsistent.  Correcting D* to the site gives 3.88 m and does not fix the band; using the case-archive ambient would make the index about 51.  Before any resolution figure is relied on, the actual p/T/rho used by the LES must be documented and D* recomputed.  That work belongs with the project engineer; it also bears on checklist items 2 and 3, which this note does not decide.
33 [Heading 1] 6.  Conformance and disposition of checklist item 4
35 [Normal] Table 2 — Conformance of the present record with QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5–§7.
36 [Normal] Disposition: checklist item 4 cannot close on the present record.  The decisive reason is not that the fire mesh is too coarse — it is finer than the band’s upper bound — but that the 7.5 is measured on the background cell while the fire-region cell is 0.125 m, so the actual D*/dx is 29.9–30.1 and §5.1 is not met; and the only alternative acceptance route, the 84% Pope figure, is not supported by a traceable LES calculation in the Verification body.  The report also places the values in Appendix C and presents a three-grid table as verification, both contrary to §6.
37 [Normal] What would settle it without a new run:
38 [List Number] Project engineer (G. Selby / R. Ellsworth) to issue a Verification addendum to report rev B (rev C) before the 11/07/2025 review.  It should report Q = 30.1 MW, D* = 3.74 m recomputed (or the documented case value), dx = 0.125 m, D*/dx = 29.9 (30.1 with 3.76 m) and state plainly that the 5–10 band is exceeded on the high side and the mesh is over-resolved.  Cite the snappy log level-5 setting and the 3.00 m plume-source zone.
39 [List Number] Provide a traceable Pope calculation from the existing LES output: k_res and k_sgs at the stated probe coordinates, the averaging start and end times, the number of puffing cycles and the sample count.  The window must be at least 10 cycles (≈11.5 s at the 1.15 s period).  If the existing fields or monitor history do not contain these quantities, say so; the 84% then cannot be produced without a new LES run.
40 [List Number] Document the ambient basis actually used by the LES (p, T, rho) and recompute D* from it.  Reconcile the DWA-derived case archive with the log initialisation (T = 308.15 K).  Show the site value (D* = 3.88 m at 750 m and 35–42 °C) alongside it.
41 [List Number] Move the three-grid table to an appendix labelled as a sensitivity study; remove it from §6 and do not present it as verification or compute a GCI from it.  Move all five resolution values into §6 with the probe location and averaging window.
42 [List Number] Reviewing Engineer (M. Falk) to record the decision in two parts: (i) whether D*/dx = 29.9 is accepted as documented over-resolution under QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5.1, or treated as a nonconformance requiring revision; and (ii) whether the Pope 84% is accepted as the sole acceptance criterion under §5.2.  If either answer is no, item 4 remains open and requires either a new LES run or a written deviation approved by the Reviewing Engineer and the Owner.
43 [Normal] If the existing LES output supports the 84% with a stated window and the report is revised as above, item 4 can close on the Pope criterion even though D*/dx is above 10, because QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5 accepts either criterion alone.  If the existing output does not support it, or if you require strict compliance with the 5–10 band, the item cannot close without a new LES run.  No new run is included in this note; the production LES runs in report Appendix B are scheduled separately for Sprint 2 (10/20/2025) and are not on file.
44 [Normal] What can be reused: the fine mesh is geometrically well formed (checkMesh “Mesh OK”, maximum non-orthogonality 58.34°, maximum skewness 2.14), and the rev C geometry and refined fire-source region are usable; the boundary-condition framework can be retained, but the solver, radiation and combustion setup must be rebuilt to Modeling Standard rev 4.  What cannot be reused is the 7.5 resolution claim, the three-grid table as verification evidence, or the 84% without its supporting data.
45 [Heading 1] 7.  Scope and limitations
46 [Normal] This note decides only peer-review checklist item 4 (resolution basis).  Items 2 (regime), 3 (solver package), 5 (through-wall treatment), 6 (validation), 7 (geometry revision) and 9 (wind-pressure units) remain open and are not decided or implied to be closed here.  The report under review is draft rev B and unsealed; this note does not release it or provide a Reviewing Engineer signature.  No new run, mesh refinement, post-processing or field extraction has been performed.  The only solver log available is the steady attempt 3; no wildfire LES monitor history or wildfire LES field data were found on the file server during this review.

--- page 1 ---
THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | QA Verification Standard — Mesh & Resolution | rev 3 | Effective 07/01/2025
Document ID: CFDME-QA-VS-MR Revision: rev 3 Effective Date: 07/01/2025 Supersedes: rev 2 (Effective
03/15/2023) Author of Record: Marguerite Falk, PE — Technical Director & Reviewing Engineer, AZ PE #42798
Applies To: All CFD deliverables issued from The CFD Mechanical Engineer, LLC (The CFD ME), 4820 E River Rd,
Suite 220, Tucson, AZ 85718
1. Purpose & Scope
This standard establishes the firm's minimum requirements for demonstrating that a CFD result is grid-independent
(for steady Reynolds-averaged work) or adequately resolved (for large-eddy simulation), and specifies how the
underlying evidence must be presented in the Verification section of every deliverable that leaves the firm.
The standard applies to every project executed by The CFD ME staff and to every subcontracted deliverable
prepared on the firm's behalf, including work performed by Mulshi Simulation Labs and any other external contractor
operating under a CFD ME work order. Reviewing Engineer sign-off on the peer-review checklist requires explicit
confirmation that the requirements of this document have been met.
Revision 3 rewrites the LES portion of the standard. The rev 2 language treated the Roache/Richardson grid
convergence index (GCI) as the default verification instrument for every solve regardless of turbulence treatment.
Two internal audits and a client peer review in Q1 2025 established that the treatment is technically incorrect for
large-eddy simulation and produces verification evidence that will not survive third-party scrutiny. The corrected
treatment is set out in Sections 4 and 5.
Nothing in this standard modifies the firm's Validation QA Procedure & Acceptance Criterion
(Firm/QA/CFDME_Validation_Procedure_rev2), the firm's Modeling Standards for Fire & Buoyant Flows
apply concurrently.
2. Definitions
Grid convergence index (GCI). A quantitative estimator of numerical uncertainty attributable to spatial discretisation
error, computed from a monotonic sequence of solutions on systematically refined grids under an assumed observed
order of accuracy. Reported as a percentage band on a selected integrated quantity of interest. The GCI is defined
for solutions that converge to a unique grid-independent limit as the mesh is refined.
Plume resolution index (D*/dx). The ratio of the characteristic plume diameter D* to the representative fire-region
cell edge length dx. D* is the buoyancy-driven length scale associated with a fire heat release rate Q_dot and is
defined as
D* = ( Q_dot / ( rho_inf · cp · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^{2/5}
where rho_inf, cp and T_inf are the ambient density, specific heat and absolute temperature respectively, and g is
gravitational acceleration. The index D*/dx is the standard measure of how many cells span the buoyancy-dominated
length scale of a fire plume.
Resolved turbulent kinetic energy (k_res). The turbulent kinetic energy carried by the explicitly resolved velocity
fluctuations in a large-eddy simulation, distinct from the sub-grid-scale contribution k_sgs modelled by the closure.
The resolved fraction is defined as k_res / (k_res + k_sgs).
RANS and steady work. In this document, "RANS and steady work" means Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes
simulations run to steady state, whether solved with a pseudo-time or true-steady solver, including internal buoyant
airflow of the type in the Copperline municipal HVAC envelope. Unsteady RANS (URANS) is treated as RANS for the
purposes of Section 4.
LES. Large-eddy simulation, including the firm's reacting-fire LES stack (fireFoam with EDC combustion and fvDOM
radiation) and any non-reacting LES of atmospheric or building flow.
3. General Requirements for Verification
Every deliverable that reports a CFD result shall contain a Verification section, plainly labelled as such, appearing in
the body of the report ahead of Validation and ahead of Results. The Verification section shall state, at minimum:
, current revision, or the Units and Conversions SOP
(Firm/Standards/CFDME_Units_SOP_rev2). Where the requirements of this standard intersect those documents, all of them


--- page 2 ---
(a) The turbulence treatment used (RANS, URANS, or LES) and, for LES, the sub-grid-scale closure.
(b) The representative cell edge length dx in the region of interest, and the total cell count.
(c) The verification basis chosen from Section 4 or Section 5, together with the numerical evidence supporting that
basis.
(d) A single-sentence statement identifying which acceptance criterion has been met and by what margin.
The Verification section shall not be an appendix pointer. Numerical values that support the verification claim shall
appear in the body. Supporting figures, residual histories, and mesh-slice imagery may be relegated to an appendix
and referenced.
Verification is prerequisite to Validation. A deliverable whose Verification section is absent, incomplete, or
inconsistent with this standard shall not be released for client transmission and shall not carry a Reviewing Engineer
signature.
4. Grid Convergence Index (GCI)
The Roache/Richardson grid convergence index is the firm's verification instrument for RANS and steady work only.
GCI is not valid for LES and shall not be used to verify any large-eddy result issued from this firm.
The reason is physical. Under systematic mesh refinement, an LES does not converge to a unique grid-independent
solution. As the filter width narrows, energy migrates from the modelled sub-grid-scale contribution into the explicitly
resolved field; the resolved-to-modelled turbulence split changes with the mesh. A three-grid sequence of LES
solutions therefore records a change in the physical content of the simulation between grids rather than a
discretisation-error tail collapsing toward a limit. The Richardson extrapolation on which the GCI is built assumes that
limit exists. It does not exist for LES, and therefore GCI values computed from an LES three-grid study are
numerically well-formed but physically meaningless. Non-monotonic behaviour in an LES three-grid quantity of
interest is the expected signature of the changing split, not evidence of a defective mesh study.
For RANS and steady solves, the firm applies the standard Richardson formulation. Given three systematically
refined grids with representative cell sizes h_1 < h_2 < h_3, refinement ratios r_21 = h_2 / h_1 and r_32 = h_3 / h_2
each at least 1.3, and a scalar quantity of interest phi with values phi_1, phi_2, phi_3 on the three grids, the observed
order of accuracy p is obtained from
phi_3 − phi_2 = ( r_32^p − 1 ) / ( r_21^p − 1 ) · ( phi_2 − phi_1 )
solved for p by fixed-point iteration. The fine-grid GCI on the finest pair is then
GCI_fine = F_s · | ( phi_2 − phi_1 ) / phi_1 | / ( r_21^p − 1 )
with a safety factor F_s of 1.25 when three or more grids are used. Reported GCI values shall carry the safety factor
and the observed p, and shall state the quantity of interest to which they apply. Monotonic convergence is a
precondition for reporting a GCI; oscillatory or divergent triples shall be flagged and the mesh study extended rather
than reported as a GCI band.
The requirement in this Section 4 applies without exception in the RANS envelope. Verification of a steady RANS
solve without a reported GCI (or an equivalent Roache/Richardson estimator) is not accepted.
5. LES Resolution Acceptance
For large-eddy simulations, the firm accepts either of the following as sufficient evidence that the resolution is
adequate in the fire or plume region of interest. Both are preferred; either alone is acceptable.
5.1 Plume resolution index. The plume resolution index D*/dx, computed with D* from the definition in Section 2 and
dx taken as the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region, shall fall in the band 5 to 10.
Values below 5 are insufficient to carry the buoyancy-driven length scale; values above 10 are wasteful of compute
without corresponding gain in fidelity for the classes of fires the firm simulates. Q_dot in the D* expression is the fire
heat release rate applied in the LES, in watts.
5.2 Pope resolved-TKE criterion. The resolved turbulent kinetic energy shall be at least 80% of the total turbulent
kinetic energy in the region of interest, i.e.
k_res / ( k_res + k_sgs ) >= 0.8


--- page 3 ---
This is Pope's criterion for a well-resolved LES. The ratio shall be computed on a time-average of a statistically
converged solution window (typically ten or more integral time scales, or ten or more puffing cycles for a pool-fire-like
plume). Point probes shall be located within the buoyancy-dominated flow, not on the periphery of the domain.
Either criterion, met, is acceptable. Meeting both is preferred and is the default expectation for deliverables prepared
for authorities-having-jurisdiction or life-safety end use. Neither criterion may be evaded by asserting engineering

6. Reporting

•
The fire heat release rate Q_dot used to compute D*, with units.
•
The characteristic plume diameter D*, with units.
•
The representative cell edge length dx in the region of interest, with units.
•
The plume resolution index D*/dx as a dimensionless number.
•
The Pope resolved-TKE fraction k_res / (k_res + k_sgs) as a percentage, together with the location of the probe(s)
and the length of the averaging window.
These values shall appear in the running text or in a table in the Verification section itself. Placement of any of these
values in an appendix, with only a cross-reference in the Verification section, does not satisfy this standard.
GCI values shall not appear in LES deliverables. A three-grid table copied forward from a RANS template into an
LES report, whether or not it is accompanied by a GCI band, is a non-compliant Verification section under this
standard. If a three-grid mesh study has been carried out on an LES case for information (for example, to
demonstrate insensitivity of an integrated quantity), the tabulated values may be included in an appendix labelled as
a sensitivity study, but they shall not be presented as verification evidence and no GCI shall be computed from them.
The Verification section of a RANS or steady deliverable shall state the observed order of accuracy p, the fine-grid

Ten-year hourly meteorology from the Pima County ALERT network at the Avra Valley WUI site establishes the design exposure envelope:

The 5.4 m solid-flame length is the wind-tilted Byram length. It is shorter than the still-air Heskestad correlation at 30.1 MW / 3.0 m (which would predict ~11.5 m); this gap between the two correlations is not treated as a discrepancy.

The plume in every solved case exhibits a well-organised puffing signature at the plume base, with a puffing frequency of 0.87 Hz. or any other steady RANS buoyant solver) for the fireFoam package in any case in scope of this standard. The
steady HVAC solver family is validated for interior building airflow at metre-per-second-scale velocities without
combustion or radiation; it is not a permissible starting point for fire work.
4. Transient Behaviour and Time-Step Control
Buoyant fire plumes are not stationary flows. The plume necks, sheds, and re-forms at a characteristic frequency that
depends only on the fire diameter and gravity. The empirical Cetegen–Ahmed relationship, adopted by the firm as
normative for design fires in the buoyancy-dominated and mixed-convection regimes, gives the puffing frequency as
corresponding to a puffing period of approximately 1.15 s. Every LES run at this diameter shall be expected to display
monitor-point oscillation at this frequency; that oscillation is the signature of physically-resolved plume dynamics.
No time-invariant resolution. Because the plume oscillates at a finite, deterministic, physical frequency, no
time-invariant flow field exists that any residual-tolerance schedule can converge to.
Time-step control. Transient LES shall use adaptive time-stepping keyed to the Courant number. The following
controlDict entries are mandatory:
f = 1.5 · D^(-1/2)  Hz
with D in metres. This is a physical property of the plume, not a numerical artefact.
Worked example. For a firm-standard LES sub-domain segment of D = 3.0 m, the puffing frequency is
f = 1.5 · (3.0)^(-1/2) = 0.87 Hz

•
application fireFoam;
•
adjustTimeStep yes;
•
maxCo 0.9;
•
maxDeltaT <case-specific ceiling, typically 0.01 s>;
•
writeControl adjustableRunTime;
•
writeInterval <chosen so that at least 25 samples per puffing period are captured on
monitors>;
The writeControl adjustableRunTime setting is required so that write intervals are pegged to wall-clock time
in the simulation rather than to solver iteration count, which permits the puffing signal to be sampled at a uniform rate.
Simulated end times shall span a minimum of 20 puffing periods after the initial transient has cleared, so that
averages, spectra, and RMS quantities are formed on a statistically meaningful window. For a 3.0 m fire that is a
simulated interval of no less than approximately 23 seconds of physical time, exclusive of startup.
5. Turbulence Modeling
The turbulence closure for cases in scope of this standard is large-eddy simulation. The sub-grid-scale (SGS) closure
shall be either:
•
Dynamic Smagorinsky — with the standard Germano–Lilly dynamic procedure and a firm-default test-filter width
of twice the mesh spacing; or
•
WALE (Wall-Adapting Local Eddy-viscosity) — preferred where solid boundaries carry a significant fraction of
the thermal load, because WALE returns the correct near-wall scaling of the SGS viscosity without requiring van
Driest damping.
The choice between the two shall be recorded in the case setup memo. Static Smagorinsky with a hand-tuned
constant, k-epsilon variants applied to LES, and hybrid RANS/LES formulations are not permitted under rev 4 for
cases in scope.
Wall functions at solid boundaries shall be the OpenFOAM standard high-Reynolds treatment appropriate to the SGS
closure and the local y+ range. The mesh at solid walls shall be sized so that the first-cell y+ stays within the
recommended band for the chosen wall function across the design range of the flow, and this shall be verified after
the initial transient by inspection of the wall-shear field.
6. Multi-Region Conjugate Heat Transfer for Cavity-Wall Assemblies
Fire-exposed building assemblies in the firm's project portfolio are commonly double-wythe (double-leaf) cavity
constructions with a solid outer leaf, an internal air cavity, and a solid inner leaf. The two leaves are typically
connected by discrete metallic ties (galvanized-steel truss ties or comparable) at regular vertical spacing, embedded
some distance into each leaf. These ties are a metallic thermal bridge across the assembly and, in ASTM E119
practice, they set the single-point temperature-rise criterion.
For any such assembly under a design fire, the CFD case shall be a multi-region conjugate heat transfer setup,
not a single-region simulation with lumped-wall boundary conditions. The following region topology is mandatory:
1. Outer leaf — solid region. Temperature-dependent k, rho, cp per the firm concrete table. Cell size at the
fire-exposed face fine enough to resolve the thermal boundary layer. 2. Cavity — fluid region with participating
radiation. Air properties temperature-dependent; radiation solved with fvDOM as in Section 3; cavity emissivities set
from the firm assembly library. 3. Inner leaf — solid region. Same treatment as the outer leaf. 4. Ties — each metallic
tie is a separate solid region, geometrically embedded through both leaves and terminating in the cavity air. Ties are
not represented as a smeared conductivity on the leaf regions and are not omitted. Steel k, rho, cp are
temperature-dependent over the design temperature range.
Region-to-region coupling at every solid–solid and solid–fluid interface shall use the OpenFOAM chtMultiRegion*

56-Regime classification.  Classification against the Modeling Standard §2 thresholds, and solver selection per §3 of that standard, shall be carried out and documented in the case setup record before any case in this matrix is meshed.
57-This classification is made once, at the firm level, for the entire Phase 1 wildfire matrix; it is not re-argued case-by-case within the envelope.
58-5.  LES Sub-Domain
59-The LES sub-domain represents a 3.0 m segment of the flaming front. This segment length is the characteristic source width used for the plume model, and the value of D_char used in the Section 4 Froude computation and in the plume-length-scale computation below.
60:5.1  Line vs Axisymmetric Reconciliation
61:The Byram fireline-intensity relation of Section 3 gives an intensity per unit length of the fire front (kW/m). The plume length scale D* referred to by the firm modeling and verification standards is an axisymmetric-source property (kW total). The two quantities are not interchangeable and cannot be composed directly. The 3.0 m segment length is the specific conversion factor between them for this project: it defines how much fire-front length is captured within one LES sub-domain, and therefore what total heat release rate the plume model sees.
62-Design fire heat release rate for the sub-domain:
63-Q = I × L_segment
64-  = (10,040 kW/m) × (3.0 m)
65-  = 30,120 kW
66-  = 30.1 MW
67-Idealizations recorded so they are not misread as physical dimensions.
68-•  Flame depth and flame residence time are not resolved in this sub-domain. The flaming front is represented as an equivalent 3.0 m characteristic-diameter source patch.
69-•  The wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m from Section 3 is a wind-tilted correlation length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height. Heskestad’s still-air flame-height correlation, evaluated for the same 30.1 MW heat release rate at a 3.0 m diameter source, gives roughly 11.5 m. The 5.4 m vs 11.5 m gap between the two correlations is not treated as a discrepancy between two attempts to model the same quantity.
70:Plume characteristic diameter D*.  For Q = 30.1 MW and standard reference-atmosphere conditions (ρ_∞ = 1.204 kg/m³, c_p = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, T_∞ = 293.15 K, g = 9.81 m/s²):
71:D* = ( Q / ( rho_inf · c_p · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^(2/5)
72-   = ( 30,100 / ( 1.204 × 1.005 × 293.15 × 3.132 ) )^(2/5)
73:   = ( 27.08 )^(2/5)
74:D* = 3.76 m.

77-which confirms the plume is adequately resolved on the fine grid. LES resolution acceptance shall be assessed per the firm QA standard applicable to reacting-plume LES.
78-6.  Wall Assembly Note
79-The through-wall response of the assembly cannot be modelled as heat conduction through a single solid slab. Per the OAS-WUI-01_revC wall assembly section (Geometry/OAS_wall_assembly_section.png), the assembly is a double-wythe cavity system: two 50 mm printed-concrete leaves separated by a 205 mm open-air cavity (overall thickness 305 mm), tied together by continuous 9-gauge (3.8 mm) galvanized truss-type steel ties spaced 600 mm on centre vertically, embedded 25 mm into each leaf. The cavity carries no insulation. The architectural drawing (OAS_wall_assembly_section.png) uses the drawing-side identifier OAS-WA-305mm-DW in its title block; this refers to the same physical wall assembly as the engineering geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC used throughout the SOW, this memo, and all downstream analysis artifacts.
